719	title: "Animate graphic properties"
720	description: Use an action to move a graphic's numbers and colours over time, switch its text and pictures at a set moment, and keep some properties out of the animation.
721	---
722	
723	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
724	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
725	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
726	
727	A graphic's [properties](/graphics/properties/) can change over time, in the same way an [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip's position or fades its opacity. Use this to slide a bar's size, change an accent colour, or swap a line of text part way through a clip.
728	
729	<AtAGlance
730	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
731	  keys="⌥⌘K"
732	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, with an action selected"
733	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_graphic']}
734	/>
735	
736	## Animate with an action
737	
738	<Steps>
739	
740	1. Select the graphic clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>).
741	
742	2. With the action selected, open the **Graphic** sub-tab.
743	
744	3. In **Properties**, set the values the graphic should end at. Each row you change gets a ◆.
745	
746	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the change.
747	
748	</Steps>
749	
750	<Shot
751	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
752	  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a count of 3. The accent, size and boxed rows have a diamond in their gutter, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
753	/>
754	
755	While an action is selected, the **Properties** rows edit the action's end, not the clip. A value you set is kept as you set it, even when it equals the module's default. **Size** and **Timeline** always edit the clip, and they show ⊘.
756	
757	The graphic gets the current values on every frame, and any animation the module does for itself still runs on top.
758	
759	To stop animating a property, take it out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action). To change when the action runs, how long it takes or its curve, see [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
760	
761	## What ramps
762	
763	Numbers and colours move along the action's curve from start to end.
764	
765	**A number** arrives with decimals. Going from 64 to 129, it's 96.5 halfway, and it's never rounded or snapped to the property's step.
766	
767	**A colour** blends through OKLab, which keeps the middle of the blend clean, and its transparency blends as a separate value. `#ff0000` to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, and `#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, a half-transparent grey.
768	
769	While a property moves, every frame has to be drawn anew. A graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
770	
771	:::caution
772	A module that needs whole numbers has to round them itself, or mark the property [`animate: false`](#stop-a-property-animating). One that does neither can fail on a fraction, and `new Array(props.count)` is the usual case. Those frames draw the error card, and an export stops there.
773	:::
774	
775	## What switches
776	
777	Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures can't blend. They hold their value through the action, then change to the end's value as the action ends. Their rows say "at end".
778	
779	For a picture, choosing **None** in the pop-up means no picture from the end of the action.
780	
781	## Where an animated property starts
782	
783	An action starts from the value in force when it begins. That's the clip's own value, or what an earlier action finished on.
784	
785	If the clip holds no value for a property, the first action to name it starts from the module's default at that moment. That default is written into the clip in the same undo step, so changing the default later doesn't move the animation. A picture property with no default starts with no picture.
786	
787	Resetting the clip's own value for a property an action animates sets it to the default, so the action still has somewhere to start from.
788	
789	## Stop a property animating
790	
791	A module can mark any property with `animate: false`, and you can't then make an action animate it. It's for anything a ramp would break, such as a count, a layout mode or a data series. The bundled templates use it for counts and data series.
792	
793	The property's row shows ⊘, and it edits the clip even while an action is selected.
794	
795	If you write modules, it's one more key on the schema entry. It must be `true` or `false`, and anything else stops the module compiling. Leaving it out means `true`.
796	
797	```js
798	export const schema = {
799	  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1, animate: false },
800	};
801	```
802	
803	See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) or **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.
804	
805	## Values and the module
806	
807	Each value you put in an action is checked against the module as it is now, including any minimum and maximum, and one that doesn't fit isn't accepted. That has a few effects when the module changes after you've animated it:
808	
809	- A value already stored isn't checked again, so narrowing a range later leaves the old end value in place.
810	- If an action names a property the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate, the row shows dimmed with **⌫**. Choose it to take the property out of the action.
811	- While the module is missing or won't compile, the **Properties** section has no rows to edit, and reads "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." You can still take values out of the action with **⌫**.
812	
813	## The badge
814	
815	The **Graphic** sub-tab shows a **◆N** badge counting how many properties the selected action animates. The **Properties** section header shows the same count. See [Read the sections and sub-tabs](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-sections-and-sub-tabs).
816	
817	On the timeline, an action's band names a graphic's animated properties along with anything else the action changes, when the track is tall enough to show the label.
818	
819	## With an agent
820	
821	An agent works the same way. It calls [`add_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#add_action), then [`set_action_end`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end) with the end values as `{graphic: {props: {…}}}`. A property set to null comes out of the action, and `graphic: null` takes them all out. It never sends the module's schema, because Frame Job reads that itself.
822	
823	It can't set a value on a property marked `animate: false` that way, and sets it on the clip with [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic) instead. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#animating-graphic-props).
824	
825	## Related

829	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)

833	title: "Paste Graphic Properties"
834	description: Copy the text, colours and other properties of one graphic clip onto other clips drawn by the same graphic, and see what stays behind.
835	---
836	
837	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
838	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
839	
840	Paste Graphic Properties copies what one graphic clip shows, its text and colours included, onto other clips drawn by the same graphic. Use it to give a run of lower thirds the same styling, then change the names.
841	
842	<AtAGlance
843	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties"
844	  tools="paste_attributes"
845	/>
846	
847	## Paste graphic properties
848	
849	<Steps>
850	
851	1. Select the graphic clip you want to copy from and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
852	
853	2. Select the clips to paste onto.
854	
855	3. Choose **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
856	
857	</Steps>
858	
859	Every selected clip drawn by the same graphic takes the copied properties, as one undo step. The menu item is on when there are Frame Job clips on the clipboard and at least one graphic clip is selected.
860	
861	## What moves and what stays
862	
863	The target ends up with exactly the copied clip's properties, so a property left at its default on the copied clip goes back to the default on the target.
864	
865	Each target keeps:
866	
867	- Its own module, size, **In** and **Length**.
868	- Its position, scale and everything else outside the **Properties** section.
869	- Any property the copied clip leaves unset and an action on the target animates, so that the action keeps its start.
870	
871	If you copied several clips, only the earliest one is read.
872	
873	## When it does nothing
874	
875	| What you'll see | Why |
876	| --- | --- |
877	| Some selected clips don't change | They're drawn by another graphic, or they aren't graphics. They're skipped. |
878	| A beep | The copied clip isn't a graphic, no selected clip is drawn by the same graphic, or the targets already match. |
879	| An alert | The copied properties can't be stored, for example more than 64 of them. It gives the reason, and nothing changes. |
880	
881	## How it differs from Paste Attributes
882	
883	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) copies a clip's look, such as its position and opacity, and never carries graphic properties. The two are separate on purpose, because a graphic's properties hold its words as well as its look.
884	
885	| | Paste Attributes | Paste Graphic Properties |
886	| --- | --- | --- |
887	| Position, scale, opacity and other picture settings | Yes | No |
888	| A graphic's text, colours and other properties | No | Yes |
889	
890	See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
891	
892	## Copy a graphic clip
893	
894	Copying and pasting a graphic clip (<kbd>⌘C</kbd>, <kbd>⌘V</kbd>) pastes a clip that names its module. The module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied.
895	
896	So in another project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card. To fix it, add the module under the same name, for example with **From File…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** on a file of that name. **From File…** also places a clip of its own, which you can delete.
897	
898	See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
899	
900	## With an agent
901	
902	An agent uses [`paste_attributes`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes) and has to ask for the graphic group by name, with `groups: ["graphic"]`, since it's never part of the default set. Unlike the menu item, a clip drawn by another graphic stops the paste with an error naming both, unless the agent sets `skip_missing` to skip those. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).
903	
904	## Related
905	
906	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
907	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
908	- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
909	- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)

2	title: "Fonts and pictures in graphics"
3	description: Add fonts and pictures to a project's graphics, find the exact font name a graphic must use, and see why a font or picture doesn't draw.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A graphic draws only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the fonts and pictures you add to the project, so it looks the same on any Mac. This page covers adding them, and what to do when one doesn't draw.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…', 'File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…']}
13	  tools={['import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'get_graphic']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Add a font
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
21	
22	2. Pick a `.ttf` or `.otf` file.
23	
24	</Steps>
25	
26	Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` folder, and every graphic in the project can then use it, straight away. Nothing is shown when it works.
27	
28	A file with the same name replaces the old one. If the file holds no font Frame Job can load, an alert says so and nothing is added.
29	
30	## Use the exact family name
31	
32	A graphic names its fonts in its code, and the bundled templates have no font property. So to use a font you've added, [edit the module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and write the family's name in `font-family`.
33	
34	That name must be the one Frame Job reads from the font file, which can differ from the name Font Book or other apps show.
35	
36	If a font doesn't draw, select the clip and open **Source** in the **Graphic** sub-tab. Under "Checked at the clip's first frame" it reports the missing family and lists every family the project has, so you can read the exact name there. The section's header shows "1 warning" when there's something to read.
37	
38	The check looks at the clip's first frame only, so a font used later in the animation isn't reported there.
39	
40	## Bundled fonts
41	
42	These seven families draw on every Mac, with nothing to install.
43	
44	| Family | Weights |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| Anton | 400 |
47	| Bebas Neue | 400 |
48	| Darker Grotesque | Variable, 300 to 900 |
49	| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
50	| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
51	| Source Sans 3 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
52	| Source Serif 4 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
53	
54	## Generic families
55	
56	A module can also ask for a generic family, which draws in a bundled face.
57	
58	| Generic | Draws in |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| `serif` | Source Serif 4 |
61	| `sans-serif` | Source Sans 3 |
62	| `monospace` | IBM Plex Mono |
63	
64	Write a generic without quotes, as in `font-family="sans-serif"`. With quotes it names a family called "sans-serif", which isn't there. `cursive` and `fantasy` aren't available.
65	
66	## System fonts
67	
68	Graphics never use the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere. To use one of them, add its file to the project with [Add Font to Graphics](#add-a-font).
69	
70	What happens to a family name in a module:
71	
72	- A family the project doesn't have draws nothing, with a warning naming the families it does have.
73	- In a list such as `"Nope, Montserrat"`, the first family the project has draws.
74	- A family with a word starting with a digit must be quoted, as in `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`. Unquoted, it draws nothing, with a warning.
75	
76	:::note
77	[Text clips](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) work differently, and do use the fonts on your Mac.
78	:::
79	
80	## Add a picture
81	
82	<Steps>
83	
84	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
85	
86	2. Pick a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file.
87	
88	</Steps>
89	
90	Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/assets/` folder. A [picture property's](/graphics/properties/) pop-up then lists it, and a module can draw it by name with `<image href="${asset(name)}">`.
91	
92	A file with the same name replaces the old one. Any other kind of file can't be added, and an empty file gets an alert and isn't added.
93	
94	## Picture names
95	
96	A module refers to a picture by its file name, and some names can't be used that way. A name is not usable when it:
97	
98	- Starts with `.` or `#`.
99	- Holds any of `/ : " ' < > &`, or a control character.
100	- Is longer than 247 bytes.
101	
102	A picture with a name like that is added under a legal one, and a notice tells you which:
103	
104	> `"#logo&mark.png" was added as "logo-mark.png": asset(name) cannot use the name it had.`
105	
106	If the legal name is taken, the picture takes `-2`, `-3` and so on, as in `logo-mark-2.png`. A renamed copy never replaces an existing file.
107	
108	## Drop files in the folder
109	
110	You can also put fonts and pictures straight into `graphics/fonts/` and `graphics/assets/` with the Finder or any other tool. Frame Job notices within a moment.
111	
112	To find the folder, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the **Source** section of a graphic clip. It shows the module's file inside `graphics/`. If `fonts` or `assets` isn't there yet, make a folder with exactly that name.
113	
114	These are skipped, with a warning in **Source** under "In the graphics folder":
115	
116	- A font that doesn't load.
117	- An empty picture.
118	- A picture with a name a module can't use. Unlike a picture added from the menu, it isn't renamed for you.
119	
120	A file of any other kind is ignored, with no warning.
121	
122	## Good to know
123	
124	- Neither import is an undo step. To take a file out, delete it from the folder.
125	- Fonts and pictures belong to the project. Another project needs its own copy.
126	- Both menu items work as soon as the project window is open. There's no need to save first.
127	
128	## With an agent
129	
130	An agent can read the exact family names directly, rather than waiting for a warning. [`get_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#get_graphic) lists them, and [`import_graphic_font`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#import_graphic_font) returns the names a new file adds. [`import_graphic_asset`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#import_graphic_asset) can file a picture under a `name` you give it, and returns the name to use, including any legal name it had to choose. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
131	
132	## Related
133	
134	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
135	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
136	- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
137	- [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/)

139	title: "Edit a module"
140	description: "Change a graphic's code in any editor, see the result as soon as you save, read what went wrong, and find the versions Frame Job kept."
141	---
142	
143	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
144	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
145	
146	A module is the JavaScript file that draws a graphic. It's an ordinary file in your project, so you can edit it in any editor, and Frame Job redraws as soon as you save.
147	
148	<AtAGlance
149	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…']}
150	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Open in Editor', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder']}
151	  tools={['get_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'render_graphic', 'render_frame', 'graphic_reference']}
152	/>
153	
154	## Edit in any editor
155	
156	<Steps>
157	
158	1. Select a graphic clip and open the **Graphic** sub-tab of the **Clip** tab.
159	
160	2. Open the **Source** section and choose **Open in Editor**. The module opens in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files.
161	
162	3. Change the code and save. The preview redraws within a moment.
163	
164	</Steps>
165	
166	To use a different editor, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the same section and open the file from there.
167	
168	The file is `graphics/<name>.js` inside your `.framejob` project package, and **Reveal in Finder** takes you straight to it. Your own scripts and tools can write to that folder too, and fonts in `graphics/fonts/` and pictures in `graphics/assets/` are watched the same way. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). The folder appears the first time something is written to it.
169	
170	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, and at most 63 characters. A `.js` file with any other name is skipped, and the **Source** section lists it under **In the graphics folder**.
171	
172	To write a module from scratch, see [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) and [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
173	
174	:::caution
175	Every clip drawn by a module changes when you edit it. To change one clip's look, use [Duplicate as New Graphic…](/graphics/manage-graphics/#duplicate-as-new-graphic) first.
176	:::
177	
178	## Live reload
179	
180	Frame Job watches the graphics folder, so you never reimport anything. When a module, a font or a picture changes:
181	
182	- The paused preview redraws.
183	- The inspector updates, including a property list the module's new code changed.
184	- A playing preview picks the change up on its next frame.
185	
186	Changes are gathered over about 100 ms, so a burst of saves lands as one.
187	
188	A save isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. **Edit ▸ Undo** won't take your code back, but [kept versions](#kept-versions) will.
189	
190	## Diagnostics
191	
192	The **Source** section reports what the module says about the selected clip, grouped under headings. Its header shows the number of errors or warnings, or the module's display name when all is well, so you can read it with the section closed.
193	
194	| Heading | What's under it |
195	| --- | --- |
196	| **Compiling the module** | The compile error, or the warnings the module's top level gave. |
197	| **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** | Nothing. That frame drew cleanly. |
198	| **Checked at the clip's first frame** | What drawing that frame reported, such as a missing font or a picture that isn't in the project. |
199	| **In the graphics folder** | Files the folder scan skipped (a bad module or picture name, an empty picture, a font that loads no face) or couldn't watch. Each has a **Reveal** button. |
200	
201	Each row reads like "line 12, column 4 — message". Click the row, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor.
202	
203	Every problem is one of two kinds:
204	
205	- An **error** means nothing drew.
206	- A **warning** means the graphic drew anyway.
207	
208	The line and column are the module's own, when they're known. Some things to know when reading them:
209	
210	- For a timeout, they point at where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
211	- Some problems found while drawing name the frame in their message, such as "render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?".
212	- A warning from the module's top level, such as `asset("x")` outside `render` when `x` isn't in `graphics/assets/`, has no frame. It comes with the compile, and the module still compiles.
213	
214	**Help ▸ Graphics Reference** sets out the same rules under **Diagnostics**.
215	
216	The inspector only checks the clip's first frame. A problem that starts later shows up as the error card when the playhead reaches it.
217	
218	When the module file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are dimmed, **Revision** reads "missing", and the section shows `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`. When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, **Source** names them and asks you to select one module's clips.
219	
220	## The error card
221	
222	A graphic that fails draws an error card in its own box, in place of the graphic. The card is dark red with a 2 px bright red border and white monospaced text. You'll see it in the preview and in stills.
223	
224	It appears for:
225	
226	- a missing module
227	- a module that doesn't compile
228	- an error your code throws
229	- a frame that runs out of time, which is 250 ms in the preview
230	- a frame whose picture can't be made
231	
232	The card reads, line by line:
233	
234	```text
235	lower-third · frame 42
236	render returned undefined at frame 42 — did you forget `return`?
237	```
238	
239	Its first line is the module's name and the frame, or `lower-third · does not compile`. The message follows, then a line such as `line 7, column 3` when the position is known. The frame number is the graphic's own, counted from its first frame.
240	
241	An error card never reaches a movie. An export [stops instead](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/#when-a-graphic-fails-partway).
242	
243	## Kept versions
244	
245	Whenever Frame Job sees a module's code replaced while the project is open, it keeps the code that was there. The last 10 versions of each module are kept.
246	
247	| Code is kept when | Code isn't kept when |
248	| --- | --- |
249	| You save from your editor | The file changes while the project is closed |
250	| An agent writes the module | Something other than Frame Job removes the file |
251	| You restore a version | |
252	| You delete the module | |
253	
254	The code the module holds now is never in the list, and code kept twice is listed once.
255	
256	To go back, choose **File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…**. See [Restore Graphic Version](/graphics/manage-graphics/#restore-graphic-version).
257	
258	Kept versions live in `graphics/history/` and travel with every save. Leave that folder to Frame Job. Fonts and pictures aren't versioned.
259	
260	## API.md and API.d.ts
261	
262	Frame Job keeps two files in `graphics/` for an editor or an agent working in the folder: `API.md`, the reference, and `API.d.ts`, its TypeScript definitions.
263	
264	They never create the folder. When the folder exists, Frame Job writes them as it opens the project and each time it writes a module, replacing either file if it differs from its own copy, so any edit you make to them is lost.
265	
266	**Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens the same reference in your default Markdown app, with or without a project open.
267	
268	## How many files are watched
269	
270	Frame Job watches the graphics folder itself, its `fonts/` and `assets/` folders, and the first 16 files one by one: modules first, then fonts, then pictures, each in name order.
271	
272	That only matters in a folder with more than 16 files. An editor that saves by swapping in a new file is always seen. A save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.
273	
274	## Good to know
275	
276	- In an untitled project, graphics live in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save. A file you already have open in an editor is left at the old path, so choose **Open in Editor** again after saving.
277	- Saves less than about 100 ms apart count as one, so only the code from before the burst is kept.
278	
279	## With an agent
280	
281	An agent reads a module with [`get_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#get_graphic) and writes one with [`write_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#write_graphic), or edits the folder with its own file tools. `write_graphic` compiles the code as it writes it and returns the result, so an agent sees each problem's level, message, line, column and frame straight away. A module that doesn't compile comes back as a list of problems to fix, not as a failed call. [`render_frame`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#render_frame) and [`render_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#render_graphic) show it the error card and report what went wrong.
282	
283	See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) and [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
284	
285	## Related
286

288	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
289	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)

293	title: "Rename, delete and restore graphics"
294	description: "Rename a module and every clip follows, delete one no clip uses, bring back kept code, and copy a module to change one clip's look."
295	---
296	
297	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
298	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
299	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
300	
301	Each graphic in a project is a module, a file of code that any number of clips can share. These commands look after those files: rename one, delete one, go back to earlier code, or split a clip off onto its own copy.
302	
303	<AtAGlance
304	  menu={['File ▸ Rename Graphic…', 'File ▸ Delete Graphic…', 'File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…']}
305	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Duplicate as New Graphic…"
306	  tools={['rename_graphic', 'delete_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'set_graphic']}
307	/>
308	
309	The three **File** items have no keyboard shortcut. Each opens a small sheet with a **Graphic:** pop-up.
310	
311	## Rename Graphic
312	
313	Renaming a module changes its file name, and every clip drawn by it follows the new name, on the timeline and inside nests.
314	
315	<Steps>
316	
317	1. Choose **File ▸ Rename Graphic…**. The sheet opens on the selected clip's module when one clip is selected, otherwise on the first module.
318	
319	2. Pick the module from **Graphic:** if it's a different one. The **New name:** field starts with the chosen module's name, and changes when you pick another.
320	
321	3. Type the new name and choose **Rename**.
322	
323	</Steps>
324	
325	<Shot
326	  name="15b-rename-graphic-sheet.sheet"
327	  alt="The Rename Graphic sheet. A paragraph explains that every clip follows the new name and how to rename back. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third, and New name: is a field holding the same name. Bottom left, small grey text reads lowercase letters, digits and -. Bottom right are Cancel and a dimmed Rename."
328	/>
329	
330	A name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, and at most 63 characters. **Rename** stays dimmed until the name isn't empty and differs from the current one.
331	
332	The module's [kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions) move with it. If the new name belonged to a deleted module, the two sets of versions join under that name. Past 10, the oldest are dropped for good, and those are the deleted module's.
333	
334	The item is dimmed in a project with no graphics and while a nest is open, because a rename reaches every clip in the project. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> first.
335	
336	## Undo a rename
337	
338	When a clip uses the module, a rename is one undo step, **Rename Graphic**. **Edit ▸ Undo** puts the clips back and moves the module's file back to its old name with them, and **Edit ▸ Redo** moves both forward again.
339	
340	A module no clip uses makes no undo step. To go back, rename it again.
341	
342	Frame Job remembers the last 32 renames in a project to do this. An undo further back than that can leave a clip naming a module that has no file, and the clip draws the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card).
343	
344	## Delete Graphic
345	
346	Deleting removes a module that no clip uses. Its code is kept, so you can bring it back.
347	
348	<Steps>
349	
350	1. Delete the clips drawn by the module, or switch them to another one. See [Switch clips to another module](#switch-clips-to-another-module).
351	
352	2. Choose **File ▸ Delete Graphic…**. The sheet always opens on the first module in the list.
353	
354	3. Pick the module from **Graphic:** and choose **Delete**.
355	
356	</Steps>
357	
358	<Shot
359	  name="15c-delete-graphic-sheet.sheet"
360	  alt="The Delete Graphic sheet. A paragraph explains that a graphic clips still use cannot be deleted, that its code is kept so Restore Graphic Version brings it back, and that deleting is not an Undo step. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third. Bottom right are Cancel and a blue Delete."
361	/>
362	
363	**Delete** is the only confirmation. There's no second question, and deleting isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited.
364	
365	Clips count wherever they are, on the timeline or in a nest. Fonts and pictures are left alone. The item is dimmed in a project with no graphics.
366	
367	## Switch clips to another module
368	
369	The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy. To move clips to an existing module, delete the clips and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again, or ask an agent to do it.
370	
371	## Restore Graphic Version
372	
373	Restoring puts back the newest kept version of a module's code, and it works on deleted modules too.
374	
375	<Steps>
376	
377	1. Choose **File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…**. The sheet opens on the selected clip's module when one clip is selected and that module has a kept version, otherwise on the first in the list.
378	
379	2. Pick the module from **Graphic:**. The pop-up lists every name with a kept version, and a deleted one reads like `lower-third (deleted)`. Under it, the sheet says how many are kept, such as "3 versions kept".
380	
381	3. Choose **Restore**.
382	
383	</Steps>
384	
385	<Shot
386	  name="15d-restore-graphic-version-sheet.sheet"
387	  alt="The Restore Graphic Version sheet. A paragraph explains that it puts back the newest kept version, keeps the code it replaces, and is not an Undo step. Graphic: is a pop-up reading lower-third, with 1 version kept in small grey type under it. Bottom right are Cancel and a blue Restore."
388	/>
389	
390	There's no list of versions to pick from. The sheet always restores the newest.
391	
392	The code a restore replaces is kept in its turn, and it becomes the newest. So restoring again returns to where you were, and the sheet swaps between those two rather than stepping further back. An agent can ask for any kept version.
393	
394	Restoring isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. The item is dimmed when no version of any graphic is kept. For when a version is kept, see [Kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions).
395	
396	## Duplicate as New Graphic
397	
398	Clips that share a module all change when it does. This writes a copy of the module under a new name and switches the selected clips to it, so you can change one clip's look and leave the rest alone.
399	
400	<Steps>
401	
402	1. Select the clips to split off.
403	
404	2. In the **Source** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab, choose **Duplicate as New Graphic…**.
405	
406	3. Type a module name. The field suggests `<name>-copy`, or `<name>-copy-2` and so on when that's taken.
407	
408	4. Choose **Duplicate**.
409	
410	</Steps>
411	
412	Writing the copy can't be undone, but switching the clips can, as one step, **Duplicate Graphic**. Undo puts the clips back on the original and leaves the copy in the folder. Use [Delete Graphic](#delete-graphic) to remove it.
413	
414	The button is dimmed when the module file is missing. When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, **Source** doesn't offer it.
415	
416	## When Frame Job won't do it
417	
418	On success, a sheet closes without a message. When Frame Job can't do what you asked it beeps, shows the reason in the sheet in its own words, and the sheet stays open so you can change your choice or choose **Cancel**.
419	
420	| Item | The sheet says | What it means |
421	| --- | --- | --- |
422	| Rename | `graphic name "My Title" is not a module name…` | The name breaks the rule above. |
423	| Rename | `graphics/title.js already exists` | Another module has that name. |
424	| Rename | `The name "title" is already drawn by clip 4 on the timeline…` | Clips left behind by a deleted module still use that name. Delete those clips or switch them first. |
425	| Delete | `The graphic "title" is still drawn by clips 4 and 9 on the timeline and clip 12 in nest 7…` | The sheet names every clip that uses it. Delete them or switch them to another module first. |
426	| Restore | `…was changed outside Frame Job and no longer holds the revision in its name; it is not restored…` | The kept file doesn't match what Frame Job stored, so nothing is written. |
427	
428	**Duplicate as New Graphic…** reports the same two naming problems in an alert. Its clips stay as they were.
429	
430	## With an agent
431	
432	[`rename_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#rename_graphic), [`delete_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#delete_graphic) and [`restore_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#restore_graphic) do what the sheets do, and give the same reasons when they can't. `restore_graphic` can name any kept version, not only the newest.
433	
434	An agent duplicates a graphic with [`write_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#write_graphic) of the module's code under the new name, then [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic). `set_graphic` can also point clips at a module that already exists, which the inspector can't do. An agent can't rename a module while a nest is open either.
435	
436	See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/) and [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
437

446	description: "Use a graphic as a matte so your footage plays through the shape it draws, and animate that shape like any other graphic."
447	---
448	
449	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
450	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
451	
452	A graphic can't read a video's pixels, but it can shape one. Make the graphic's track a matte and the video behind it shows only where the graphic draws, or, inverted, only where it doesn't.
453	
454	<AtAGlance
455	  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
456	  tools={['set_track']}
457	/>
458	
459	## Show video inside a graphic
460	
461	<Steps>
462	
463	1. Put the video on a track, and the graphic on the track directly above it. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
464	
465	2. Line the graphic clip up with the stretch of video you want cut. Where the matte track has no clip, the video shows uncut.
466	
467	3. Select the graphic clip.
468	
469	4. Choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Alpha**.
470	
471	</Steps>
472	
473	The graphic itself is no longer drawn. What it shows now decides where the video can be seen. To go back, choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Off**.
474	
475	## Choose a mode
476	
477	| Mode | The video shows where the graphic is |
478	| --- | --- |
479	| **Alpha** | Opaque |
480	| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
481	| **Luma** | Bright |
482	| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |
483	
484	**Off** makes it an ordinary track again.
485	
486	## Write a module for a matte
487	
488	A matte module is written and called exactly like any other, and the cut follows each frame as it animates. Fill the window in white so it works in every mode.
489	
490	This one opens a rounded window with a spring:
491	
492	```js
493	export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
494	export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };
495	
496	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
497	  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
498	  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
499	  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
500	  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
501	    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
502	}
503	```
504	
505	Its **radius** property appears on the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/) as usual, and you can [animate it](/graphics/animate-properties/). See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
506	
507	## What the clip's settings still do
508	
509	The graphic clip's position, scale, rotation, opacity and actions still shape the window, so you can move or fade it with the same controls as any clip.
510	
511	Its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. They're kept, and they apply again if the track stops being a matte.
512	
513	The video's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape.
514	
515	## Good to know
516	
517	Only the track directly behind the matte is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) has the whole story, including what happens with two matte tracks in a row and how a matte looks on the timeline.
518	
519	## With an agent
520	
521	[`set_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track) sets a track's `matte` to `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`, and `none` turns it off. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#track-mattes).
522

530	title: "Graphics playback and memory"
531	description: "How Frame Job keeps heavy graphics playing smoothly: drawing ahead, kept frames, Background render, and the memory they're allowed to use."
532	---
533	
534	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
535	
536	A graphic is drawn from code, frame by frame, and a heavy one can take longer to draw than a frame lasts. Frame Job works around that by drawing ahead of the playhead and keeping what it has drawn. Nearly all of this is automatic, and the one thing you can set is [Background render](#background-render).
537	
538	<AtAGlance
539	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback"
540	  keys="⌘,"
541	/>
542	
543	## Drawing ahead while playing
544	
545	While a preview plays forward over a project with a graphic in it, on the timeline or in a nest, Frame Job draws upcoming frames on spare processor cores ahead of the playhead. It uses one fewer core than your Mac has active.
546	
547	It starts again from the new spot on play, on a seek, and on an edit while playing. It runs to the end of the timeline, or to the end of the in and out range while playback is looping inside it.
548	
549	It doesn't run while the preview is paused or playing in reverse. Background render covers paused.
550	
551	## Kept frames
552	
553	A window keeps the graphic frames it has drawn in memory while it's open, so a stretch you play again comes from memory rather than being drawn again.
554	
555	A frame is matched by what it draws, so changing a module or a property only redraws the frames that come out different. Frames go when the window closes or newer frames replace them. The least recently used go first, and frames Background render drew ahead give way last.
556	
557	## Background render
558	
559	When you leave Frame Job alone, the window you last played or moved the playhead in draws its graphics ahead of the paused playhead, so the next play is smooth from the start.
560	
561	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
562	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
563	| **Background render** | Turns background drawing on or off. | On | |
564	| **Start after … seconds** | How long Frame Job must be left alone first. | 5 | 1 to 60 |
565	
566	Find them in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback**. They save the moment you change them, with no **Save** button, and they apply to every project. The ⓘ on the **Playback** heading explains them.
567	
568	Background render needs a paused window that draws a graphic. It draws from the playhead to the end of the timeline, or to the end of the in and out range while playback would loop inside it, and it ends early if the [memory budget](#the-memory-budget) runs out. After that it waits for your next activity and the same wait before it runs again.
569	
570	It keeps the processor busy while it runs, and it carries on while Frame Job is hidden or covered. It doesn't stop your Mac going to sleep. It only draws graphic frames, and it changes nothing in your project or your export.
571	
572	## Set how long it waits
573	
574	**Start after … seconds** takes a whole number from 1 to 60, typed or with the stepper. You can only change them while **Background render** is on. A typed number outside the range beeps and the stored value comes back.
575	
576	## What stops Background render
577	
578	Any activity in Frame Job stops the pass at once, and it starts again after the same wait.
579	
580	| Stops it | Doesn't stop it |
581	| --- | --- |
582	| A key, including a modifier key on its own | Moving the pointer |
583	| A click, a drag, a scroll or a trackpad gesture | Working in another app |
584	| Any edit, in any window | An agent's read-only call, such as `get_project` |
585	| Play, pause or a seek, in any window | |
586	| An agent's call that edits a project or moves a playhead | |
587	
588	It never runs while any window is playing.
589	
590	## The memory budget
591	
592	The frames drawn ahead and the frames kept share one budget for all of Frame Job. It's sized to your Mac, with no fixed cap in gigabytes.
593	
594	| Memory on your Mac | Budget |
595	| --- | --- |
596	| Normal | A quarter of its physical memory, so 8 GB on a 32 GB Mac |
597	| Short | An eighth |
598	| Critically short | Nothing. No frames are held, and each graphic is drawn when it's needed. |
599	
600	The frames an [export](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/#parallel-rendering) draws ahead count too. Frames being drawn ahead come first, and kept frames give up whatever room those need.
601	
602	Each playing window or export also holds at most 1,024 pictures ahead, however much memory is free.
603	
604	## What Frame Job skips
605	
606	Frame Job also avoids repeating work it has already done, in two ways.
607	
608	### Repeat frames
609	
610	When a frame's SVG is the same as one already drawn, such as during a hold or in a static graphic, Frame Job reuses that picture. Your module still runs for every frame. Only the drawing of its SVG into a picture is skipped.
611	
612	While an [action](/graphics/animate-properties/) moves a property that changes what the module draws, every frame comes out different, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action.
613	
614	### The picture cache
615	
616	PNG and JPEG pictures a graphic draws are decoded once and cached, so graphics full of pictures draw faster. The result is identical to drawing the original.
617	
618	The cache is a sixteenth of the graphics budget, so it shrinks when memory is short. The least recently used go first.
619	
620	## Good to know
621	
622	Your module's code has 250 ms to run for each frame in the preview. Past that the frame draws the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card). An export allows 2 s, so a frame that fails in the preview can still export. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
623	
624	Background render is a setting for a person. No agent tool reads or writes it.
625

633	title: "Graphics in exports"
634	description: "What an export draws for each graphic, what stops an export when one is broken, and where a graphic's warnings show up."
635	---
636	
637	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
638	
639	An export draws each graphic the way the preview does, so the file matches what you saw. A broken graphic never reaches the file: the export stops and tells you which one and why.
640	
641	<AtAGlance
642	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
643	  keys="⌘E"
644	  tools={['export', 'export_status']}
645	/>
646	
647	## What an export draws
648	
649	An export draws each graphic as its module stood when you started or queued the export, whatever you edit next. Editing a module while an export runs doesn't change that file, and a job waiting in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) draws the code it was queued with.
650	
651	So you can carry on working on a module while an export runs. To get your new code into a file, export again.
652	
653	## Parallel rendering
654	
655	An export draws its graphics ahead on worker threads, one fewer than your Mac's active cores, so a graphics-heavy export doesn't wait on one frame at a time. The file is the same as drawing them one at a time.
656	
657	It isn't used for an animated GIF or APNG, for a single frame, or for an audio-only export. Frames drawn ahead share the [memory budget](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#the-memory-budget) with the preview's.
658	
659	## When a graphic won't compile
660	
661	An export that would draw a graphic whose module is missing or doesn't compile isn't started, and any file already at that path is left alone. The message names each graphic and its first error:
662	
663	> The export was not started: the graphic "logo" has no module in graphics/; the graphic "title" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again.
664	
665	The check covers every graphic clip in the export's range, and every graphic in each nest reached from those clips. That's the whole nest, not only the part the export plays, so a broken graphic elsewhere in a nest stops the export too.
666	
667	An audio-only export isn't checked, because it draws no pictures.
668	
669	A job in the Export Queue reports this in its row when its turn comes, and it keeps the code it was queued with. Fix the module and export again.
670	
671	## When a graphic fails partway
672	
673	Compiling is the only check made before an export starts. A graphic that throws at frame 900 is found at frame 900. A graphic that fails partway through stops the export at that frame, and no file is left behind:
674	
675	> The export was stopped at frame 900 of the graphic "title": … No file was written.
676	
677	The frame number is the graphic's own, counted from its first frame. A frame fails when your code throws, when your code takes more than 2 s on it, or when its picture can't be made.
678	
679	To find a failure before a long export, play the graphic through in the preview and watch for the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card). Your code has only 250 ms a frame there, so the preview is the stricter of the two. A frame whose code takes between 250 ms and 2 s shows the card in the preview and exports normally.
680	
681	## Warnings in a finished export
682	
683	Warnings a graphic gives while drawing don't stop the export. Frame Job reports each distinct one when the file is done, with the graphic's name and the first frame it happened on.
684	
685	- The Exporting sheet's finish line adds a count, such as "1 graphic warning (hover for details)". Rest the pointer on the line to see each warning.
686	- An [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) row adds the count too, and its tooltip lists them.
687	
688	Each one reads like `"title" at frame 12: message`. A warning given on every frame counts once, and an export reports up to 64 distinct warnings.
689	
690	## The frozen clock
691	
692	The clock inside a graphic is frozen, so nothing depends on when it's drawn and an export matches the preview. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
693	
694	A graphic can't show today's date on its own, so give it the date through a [property](/graphics/properties/). A date you write out in the code, such as `new Date("2026-03-01")`, works as usual. The rest of the sandbox is on [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
695	
696	## Good to know
697	
698	**Save Frame** doesn't stop for a broken graphic. The graphic draws its error card, and the card is what's saved. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
699	
700	## With an agent
701	
702	[`export`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export) gives a broken graphic's reason straight away, before anything is queued. A failure while writing comes back from [`export_status`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export_status) as a failed job, naming the graphic and the frame, and a finished job lists any warnings under `graphic_warnings`, each with its name, frame and message. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
703

711	title: Graphics with an agent
712	description: Let an agent write a graphic module, look at its frames, place it on the timeline and check the result, and see what undo covers.
713	---
714	
715	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
716	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
717	
718	An agent is an AI tool that works in Frame Job for you, such as Claude Code connected over MCP, or the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/). You describe the graphic you want, and it can make it from start to finish: read the API, write the [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules) that draws it, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.
719	
720	Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
721	
722	<AtAGlance
723	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
724	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
725	  tools={[
726	    'graphic_reference',
727	    'write_graphic',
728	    'render_graphic',
729	    'get_graphic',
730	    'list_graphics',
731	    'insert_graphic',
732	    'add_graphic_clip',
733	    'set_graphic',
734	    'import_graphic_font',
735	    'import_graphic_asset',
736	    'add_action',
737	    'set_action_end',
738	    'render_frame',
739	  ]}
740	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab with your Anthropic key."
741	/>
742	
743	## The loop
744	
745	<Steps>
746	
747	1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` returns it. An agent reads it once, before writing a graphic.
748	
749	2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` saves the module, compiles it and says whether that worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.
750	
751	3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.
752	
753	4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The reply to a font import gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the reply to a picture import gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
754	
755	5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
756	
757	6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.
758	
759	</Steps>
760	
761	## Read the API
762	
763	`graphic_reference` returns the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.
764	
765	No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.
766	
767	## Write a module
768	
769	`write_graphic` saves `graphics/<name>.js` in the project, compiles that exact text and reports the result. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and the file is written in one go, so nothing ever reads half of it.
770	
771	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.
772	
773	The reply says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still a normal reply, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as an `asset()` call there that names a file the folder doesn't hold.
774	
775	Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).
776	
777	[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.
778	
779	## A contact sheet
780	
781	`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.
782	
783	| Choice | What it does | Default |
784	| --- | --- | --- |
785	| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
786	| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
787	| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
788	| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
789	| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
790	| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |
791	
792	The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.
793	
794	Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.
795	
796	A frame that fails is drawn as its [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card), and the reply adds a sentence naming the frame and the problem, with its line and column when the engine has them. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.
797	
798	A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call fails before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.
799	
800	:::note
801	The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
802	:::
803	
804	## One frame's SVG
805	
806	Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` returns one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.
807	
808	It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is an error. If the frame fails, the reply says so and holds no SVG.
809	
810	## List and insert
811	
812	`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.
813	
814	Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".
815	
816	`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.
817	
818	- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The reply names the module the clip is drawn by.
819	- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
820	- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call fails with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.
821	
822	See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
823	
824	## Place a clip
825	
826	`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also place the clip inside a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.
827	
828	| Choice | Default | Limit |
829	| --- | --- | --- |
830	| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
831	| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
832	| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |
833	
834	Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed stops the call, and the error names the property. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.
835	
836	Frame Job won't place the clip when:
837	
838	- The module isn't in the folder. The error says what the folder holds.
839	- The module doesn't compile. The error gives its first problem.
840	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The error names the key.
841	- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The error names the canvas.
842	- The clip would overlap another one on the track, as for any clip.
843	
844	## Change a clip
845	
846	`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).
847	
848	- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
849	- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
850	- **In** can't be set here. It moves when you trim the clip's front, roll the cut before it or split it.
851	
852	These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.
853	
854	Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, unless the same call names one module for them all, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.
855	
856	## Read a module or the folder
857	
858	`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. The **Source** section shows you the file, revision and problems.
859	
860	With no name it reads the folder:
861	
862	- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
863	- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
864	- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
865	- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
866	- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.
867	
868	## File tools
869	
870	An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.
871	
872	| What | Where |
873	| --- | --- |
874	| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
875	| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
876	| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |
877	
878	`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.
879	
880	A module saved a moment ago can read as not compiling, with one problem saying Frame Job hasn't compiled it yet. Ask again.
881	
882	In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.
883	
884	See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.
885	
886	## Undo rules
887	
888	The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.
889	
890	| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
891	| --- | --- | --- |
892	| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
893	| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
894	| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
895	| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |
896	
897	Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again. With no clips drawn by the module, a rename makes no undo step. `import_graphic` can't be undone either, and `export_graphic` edits nothing, so it has no undo step.
898	
899	Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 versions of each module, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's code is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
900	
901	## Graphics in render frame
902	
903	`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the reply has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
904	
905	## The Assistant
906	
907	The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It already knows a graphic is a module and where to read what a module can draw, so plain words are enough. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).
908	
909	It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.

9	A graphic is drawn by a module: one JavaScript file whose `render` function returns an SVG picture for each frame. Write your own when the [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) don't draw what you need. This page covers the shape of that file and the rules it runs under. [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) lists the helpers it can call, and **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens the whole reference. If you'd rather not write code, [an agent can write the module](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/).

17	## Try your first module
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.
22	
23	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.
24	
25	3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a valid name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.
30	
31	## The module
32	
33	A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.
34	
35	```js
36	export const meta = {
37	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
38	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
39	};
40	
41	export const schema = {
42	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
43	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
44	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
45	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
46	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
47	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
48	};
49	
50	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
51	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
52	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
53	    { clamp: true });
54	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
55	  return svg(ctx, `
56	    <g opacity="${fade}">
57	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
58	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
59	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
60	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
61	    </g>`);
62	}
63	```
64	
65	| Export | Required | What it is |
66	| --- | --- | --- |
67	| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
68	| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
69	| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |
70	
71	`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.
72	
73	`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.
74	
75	The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
76	
77	## `meta`
78	
79	Every key is optional.
80	
81	| Key | What it does |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
84	| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
85	| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
86	| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
87	| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |
88	
89	A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.
90	
91	## `ctx`
92	
93	`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.
94	
95	| Key | What it is |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
98	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
99	| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length plus anything trimmed from its front, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
100	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
101	| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
102	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |
103	
104	## Resolution-independent drawing
105	
106	Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.
107	
108	A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:
109	
110	```js
111	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
112	```
113	
114	On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
115	
116	## The schema
117	
118	The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.
119	
120	| Rule | Limit |
121	| --- | --- |
122	| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
123	| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
124	| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
125	| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |
126	
127	`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
128	
129	A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.
130	
131	## Prop types
132	
133	| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
134	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
135	| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
136	| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
137	| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
138	| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
139	| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
140	| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |
141	
142	- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
143	- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
144	- **`asset`.** A value of `""` stored on a clip reaches `render` as `null`, but a `default` of `""` reaches it as `""`, so test for an empty value before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.
145	
146	## Tolerant props
147	
148	`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.
149	
150	A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:
151	
152	```text
153	props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
154	```
155	
156	A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/#stale-values) for how those leftover values show in the inspector.
157	
158	## The SVG the engine draws
159	
160	Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg, an SVG renderer. It draws text with the fonts graphics can use, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.
161	
162	An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
163	
164	These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:
165	
166	| Warning | What to do |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
169	| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
170	| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
171	| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |
172	
173	A size mismatch warns too, but the picture still draws: `the SVG is 100×100 but the graphic is 1920×1080`. Using `svg(ctx, body)` for the root element avoids it.
174	
175	SVG that can't be read at all is an error, and starts `the SVG did not parse:`.
176	
177	## The sandbox
178	
179	A module runs in a sandbox, shut off from everything else on your Mac. A graphic can only use its `frame`, `props`, `ctx`, fonts and pictures, so the same frame with the same properties always draws the same pixels. These stop with an error:
180	
181	| In your module | The error |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| `Math.random()` | `Error: Math.random is not available; use random(seed)` |
184	| `import x from "x"` | `ReferenceError: Error resolving module 'x' from 'lower-third': imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global` |
185	| `new Function("…")` | `Error: Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code` |
186	| `eval("…")` | `ReferenceError: eval is not defined` |
187	
188	There's also no `fetch`, no file access, no clock, no `performance`, no `WebAssembly` and no `Intl`. For numbers with thousands separators, use `formatNumber`.
189	
190	`Date` is frozen. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 1 January 2000 at 00:00 UTC. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
191	
192	## Modern JavaScript
193	
194	Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`, `**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll` and `findLast`.
195	
196	## The time budget
197	
198	A runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging Frame Job, because every call has a deadline.
199	
200	| Where | Budget |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| Each frame in the preview | 250 ms |
203	| Each frame in an export | 2 s |
204	| The module's top level (the code outside `render`), when it compiles | 250 ms |
205	
206	Over the budget, you get an error such as:
207	
208	```text
209	over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError: interrupted)
210	```
211	
212	When that error gives a line and column, they're where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
213	
214	## Limits
215	
216	Each module runs in an engine of its own, with these limits:
217	
218	| Limit | Amount | Past it |
219	| --- | --- | --- |
220	| Heap | 64 MiB | An error with a line and column |
221	| Stack | 1 MiB | An error with a line and column |
222	| A graphic's side | 8192 pixels | Frame Job won't draw it |
223	| The SVG `render` returns | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) | `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most 8388608 bytes` |
224	
225	`render` must return a string that starts with `<svg`. Anything else is an error:
226	
227	| What happened | The error |
228	| --- | --- |
229	| No `return` | ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?`` |
230	| A string that isn't SVG | `render returned a string that does not start with <svg at frame 12: …` |
231	| No `render` exported | ``the module exports no `render` function`` |
232	
233	A frame that fails draws a red error card on the clip, and stops an export. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for where errors and warnings show.

256	/>
257	
258	All of these are already there when your module runs, so there's nothing to import. The examples use the arguments of `render(frame, props, ctx)`: `frame` is the frame being drawn, `props` holds the values set in the inspector, and `ctx` holds the size, frame rate and progress. [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) explains them.
259	
260	## The graphics reference
261	
262	Choose **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** to open the whole API in your default Markdown app, with or without a project open. It covers a module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, the limits and the worked examples. The menu item is dimmed only if the reference file is missing from the app.
263	
264	Frame Job also keeps two files beside your modules once a project has a graphics folder:
265	
266	| File | What it is |
267	| --- | --- |
268	| `API.md` | The same reference. |
269	| `API.d.ts` | Type definitions for the whole API, for an editor or an agent working in the folder. |
270	
271	Frame Job doesn't make a graphics folder only to hold them. Don't edit them, because Frame Job puts its own text back over any change.
272	
273	An agent reads the same reference with `graphic_reference`, which needs no project open. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
