295	## Start the frame
296	
297	### `svg()`
298	
299	`svg(ctx, body, {background})` writes the root element with the right `width`, `height` and `viewBox`, around whatever markup you pass as `body`.
300	
301	```js
302	const plain = svg(ctx, `<circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="#fff"/>`);
303	const onBlack = svg(ctx, "", { background: "#000000" });
304	```
305	
306	`background` is optional and paints the whole frame in a colour. Leave it out and the frame stays clear behind what you draw. `body` goes in exactly as you wrote it, so a prop inside it needs [`escapeXml`](#escapexml).
307	
308	## Animate values
309	
310	### `interpolate()`
311	
312	`interpolate(value, input, output, options)` maps a value through matching ranges. It's the helper most animation starts from.
313	
314	```js
315	const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 400], { clamp: true });
316	const pulse = interpolate(frame, [0, 15, 30], [1, 1.2, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutSine });
317	```
318	
319	`input` and `output` need two or more points each, and the same number of them, or the helper throws. Keep `input` ascending.
320	
321	| Option | What it does | Default |
322	| --- | --- | --- |
323	| `easing` | A curve from [`Easing`](#easing), applied inside each pair of points. | Straight line |
324	| `clamp` | With `true`, the result stops at the first and last `output` values. | `false` |
325	| `extrapolateLeft` | What happens before the first `input` point: `"extend"`, `"clamp"` or `"identity"`. | `"extend"`, or `"clamp"` when `clamp` is `true` |
326	| `extrapolateRight` | The same after the last `input` point. | `"extend"`, or `"clamp"` when `clamp` is `true` |
327	
328	Outside `input`, `"extend"` carries on along the end segment, so `interpolate(40, [0, 30], [0, 400])` gives about 533. `"identity"` returns `value` unchanged. Either `extrapolate` option wins over `clamp` on its own side.
329	
330	### `Easing`
331	
332	`Easing` holds ready-made curves to pass to `interpolate`. You can also call one directly: each takes `t` from 0 to 1 and is exact at 0 and 1.
333	
334	- `Easing.linear`
335	- `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, which makes a curve of your own
336	- `in`, `out` and `inOut` of `quad`, `cubic`, `quart`, `expo`, `sine`, `back` and `elastic`, spelled `Easing.inQuad`, `Easing.outCubic`, `Easing.inOutBack` and so on
337	
338	```js
339	const eased = Easing.outCubic(0.5);
340	const custom = Easing.bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)(0.5);
341	const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [300, 0], { easing: Easing.outBack, clamp: true });
342	```
343	
344	The `back` and `elastic` curves go past the end of their range on the way. `clamp` doesn't stop that, because it only holds the value once `input` runs out.
345	
346	### `spring()`
347	
348	`spring()` gives a physical spring from one value to another.
349	
350	```js
351	const scale = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
352	const late = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, stiffness: 180, from: 0.5, to: 1 });
353	```
354	
355	| Option | What it does | Default |
356	| --- | --- | --- |
357	| `frame` | The frame to read the spring at. | Needed |
358	| `fps` | The frame rate. Pass `ctx.fps`. | Needed |
359	| `stiffness` | How hard the spring pulls towards `to`. | 100 |
360	| `damping` | How quickly the movement dies away. | 10 |
361	| `mass` | How heavy the thing moving is. | 1 |
362	| `from` | Where it starts. | 0 |
363	| `to` | Where it settles. | 1 |
364	
365	A spring starts at frame 0 and sits at `from` before that, so `frame - 12` starts it 12 frames late. It overshoots unless it's damped: on the defaults it reaches about 1.16 on its way to 1, and with the default stiffness and mass a `damping` of 20 or more stops the overshoot. The same frame always gives the same value.
366	
367	### `interpolateColors()`
368	
369	`interpolateColors(value, input, colors)` blends colours in OKLab, a colour space built so that a blend looks even. It returns `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when any of the colours isn't fully opaque.
370	
371	```js
372	const fill = interpolateColors(frame, [0, 60], ["#ff5a36", "#3666ff"]);
373	const glass = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)", "#ffffff"]);
374	const sky = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["hsl(200, 80%, 30%)", "skyblue"]);
375	```
376	
377	`input` works as it does in `interpolate`, with two or more points and one colour for each. Outside `input` the result always holds at the end colours.
378	
379	It takes the same colours a `color` prop takes:
380	
381	| Form | Notes |
382	| --- | --- |
383	| `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa` | |
384	| `rgb()`, `rgba()` | Channels 0 to 255 or a percentage, alpha 0 to 1 or a percentage. |
385	| `hsl()`, `hsla()` | Hue in degrees, saturation and lightness as percentages. |
386	| A name | Any of the 147 CSS colour names, or `transparent`. |
387	
388	A value out of range, such as `rgb(300, 0, 0)`, throws rather than being clamped.
389	
390	## Add variation
391	
392	### `random()`
393	
394	`random(seed)` returns a number from 0 up to, but not including, 1. It depends only on the seed, which is a number or a string, so the same seed gives the same number on every frame and in every export.
395	
396	```js
397	const jitter = random(`dot-${frame}`) * 10;
398	const hue = Math.floor(random(42) * 360);
399	```
400	
401	Put the frame in the seed for a value that changes, as `jitter` does, and leave it out for one that stays. The seed is read as text, so `42` and `"42"` give the same number.
402	
403	`Math.random` isn't available in a graphic. Calling it throws "Math.random is not available; use random(seed)".
404	
405	### Noise
406	
407	`noise2D(seed, x, y)` and `noise3D(seed, x, y, z)` give simplex noise for organic motion: a value between −1 and 1 that changes smoothly as its inputs do. The seed works as it does for `random`.
408	
409	```js
410	const drift = noise2D("wave", frame / 60, 0) * 40;
411	const wobble = noise3D(7, 0.5, 0.5, ctx.time) * 20;
412	```
413	
414	For smooth drift, use `noise3D` with time as the third axis.
415	
416	## Path helpers
417	
418	These three take `d`, ordinary SVG path data. Every command works, in its absolute and relative forms: `M L H V C S Q T A Z`.
419	
420	| Helper | What it returns |
421	| --- | --- |
422	| `getLength(d)` | The path's length. Curves and arcs are measured in short straight pieces, so the answer can be a few hundredths of a percent short. |
423	| `getPointAtLength(d, length)` | `{x, y, angle}`: the point that far along, and the way the path is heading there in degrees, ready for `rotate()`. A `length` outside the path stops at its nearest end. |
424	| `evolvePath(progress, d)` | `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress` from 0 to 1. Put both on the `<path>` and it's drawn from its start up to that fraction. |
425	
426	```js
427	const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
428	const total = getLength(d);
429	const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
430	const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
431	const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
432	  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
433	  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
434	```
435	
436	`evolvePath` keeps `progress` between 0 and 1, and a closed outline closes at 1. A path of several pieces, with more than one `M`, draws them all at once, each from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1. To draw pieces one after another, give each its own `<path>`.
437	
438	A path has to start with a move, `M` or `m`. One that can't be read throws, naming where reading stopped, for example `getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"`. It's never a silent zero, though an empty `d` measures 0. A number too large to do arithmetic with, such as `1e999`, throws the same error, so you never get `Infinity` or `NaN` back.
439	
440	Frame Job remembers the paths a graphic measures, so the same `d` costs almost nothing on later calls and frames. It holds up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and measured pieces between them, where a curve is 64 pieces. Past either limit it forgets them all and measures again when asked. With paths that large, take every length and point you need from one before turning to the next.
441	
442	## Work with text
443	
444	The text helpers measure with the same fonts the graphic draws with: the ones bundled with Frame Job and any in the project, never the system's. [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) lists them.
445	
446	### `measureText()`
447	
448	`measureText(text, font)` measures text. `font` is an object, and all four text helpers read it the same way:
449	
450	| Key | What it does | Default |
451	| --- | --- | --- |
452	| `family` | The font family. | `"Montserrat"` |
453	| `size` | The size in pixels, above 0. | 16 |
454	| `weight` | The weight, 1 to 1000. | 400 |
455	| `style` | `"normal"`, `"italic"` or `"oblique"`. | `"normal"` |
456	| `letterSpacing` | Extra space between letters. | 0 |
457	| `xmlSpace` | `"default"` collapses runs of spaces, as SVG draws them. `"preserve"` counts them, as `xml:space="preserve"` draws them. | `"default"` |
458	
459	It returns `{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`. `width` is the advance, which is where the next word would start. `inkX` and `inkWidth` describe the glyphs actually drawn.
460	
461	```js
462	const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
463	const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
464	const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
465	```
466	
467	A family that isn't installed throws, naming the families that are. Any `xmlSpace` other than those two throws too. Text that's only spaces measures zero either way.
468	
469	### `wrapText()`
470	
471	`wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)` breaks text into lines that each fit `maxWidth`, and returns them as a list. A word longer than the width breaks by characters.
472	
473	```js
474	const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
475	  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
476	```
477	
478	Line breaks in the text count as spaces, so split on them first if you want to keep them.
479	
480	### `fitText()`
481	
482	`fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min, max})` returns the largest whole font size at which the text fits on one line. `min` defaults to 8 and `max` to 400, and the `size` in `font` is ignored.
483	
484	```js
485	const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
486	```
487	
488	It never goes outside `min` and `max`, so text too long to fit at `min` still comes back as `min` and runs over. Empty text returns `max`.
489	
490	### `textLines()`
491	
492	`textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})` writes a `<text>` element with one `<tspan>` per line.
493	
494	```js
495	const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
496	const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
497	  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
498	```
499	
500	| Option | What it does | Default |
501	| --- | --- | --- |
502	| `x`, `y` | Where the first line goes. | 0 |
503	| `lineHeight` | The distance between lines. | 1.2 × the size |
504	| `anchor` | `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`. | `"start"` |
505	| `fill` | The text colour. | Not written |
506	| `font` | The same `font` object as `measureText`. | |
507	
508	It does the fiddly parts for you. It quotes the family, leaving a generic such as `sans-serif` bare as it has to be. It escapes each line, so don't pass lines through `escapeXml` first. It also writes `font-style`, `letter-spacing` and `xml:space` to match the font `wrapText` broke the lines with, so what's drawn is what was measured.
509	
510	## Prepare values
511	
512	### `escapeXml()`
513	
514	`escapeXml(s)` escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, so a prop is safe to write into markup. Put every prop you write into markup through it. Without it, a title like "Tom & Jerry" stops the frame with an error that starts "the SVG did not parse".
515	
516	```js
517	const safe = escapeXml("Tom & Jerry <live>");
518	```
519	
520	The exception is text you pass to [`textLines`](#textlines), which escapes it already. Escaping twice puts `&` on screen.
521	
522	### `formatNumber()`
523	
524	`formatNumber(n, {decimals, separator})` groups thousands, because a graphic has no `Intl`. `decimals` defaults to 0 and `separator` to a comma.
525	
526	```js
527	const label = formatNumber(1234567.891, { decimals: 2 });
528	const plain = formatNumber(Math.round(interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, 5000], { clamp: true })));
529	```
530	
531	`label` here is `1,234,567.89`. The number is rounded to `decimals`, a minus sign is kept, and `NaN` or `Infinity` comes back as that word.
532	
533	## Draw a picture
534	
535	### `asset()`
536	
537	`asset(name)` returns the `href` of a file in the project's `graphics/assets/` folder, for an `<image>` element.
538	
539	```js
540	const logo = `<image href="${asset("logo.png")}" x="40" y="40" width="200" height="200"/>`;
541	```
542	
543	A name that isn't in the folder gives a warning naming the files that are, and the image doesn't draw. [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) covers adding pictures and how they're named.
544	
545	## Idioms
546	
547	The reference ends with six complete modules, each showing a common move. You can copy any of them into a graphic and it works as written. Find them under **Idioms** in **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.
548	
549	| Idiom | What it shows | The key line |
550	| --- | --- | --- |
551	| A slide-in | Text sliding in with `interpolate` and `Easing`. | `interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [-ctx.width / 2, ctx.width / 2], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true })` |
552	| A staggered list | Rows springing in one after another. | `spring({ frame: frame - i * 6, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 })` |
553	| A counter | A number counting up. | `formatNumber(Math.round(value)) + props.suffix` |
554	| Fit and wrap a title | A title sized and wrapped to the frame. | `fitText(props.title, maxWidth * 2, base, { min: 48, max: 220 })`, then `wrapText` and `textLines` |
555	| A draw-on stroke | A line drawing itself. | `evolvePath(drawn, d)` |
556	| Follow a path | An arrowhead following a curve. | `getPointAtLength(d, getLength(d) * drawn)`, then `rotate(${tip.angle})` |
557	
558	All six work out their positions and sizes from `ctx`, so the same module draws at any size. The exception is the `min` and `max` in Fit and wrap a title, which are fixed sizes. A slide-in and A staggered list scale everything by this unit, which also keeps a portrait canvas from drawing too big:
559	
560	```js
561	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
562	```

653	## How long a template runs
654	
655	The default length is in frames at your project's frame rate, so a 150-frame template is 5 seconds in a 30 fps project and 2.5 seconds in a 60 fps one.
656	
657	To change how long a graphic runs, drag the clip's end on the timeline. [**Follow Clip**](/graphics/size-and-timing/#follow-clip) is on for a new clip, so the exit moves with the clip's end and the entrance still plays from the first frame. A few templates also time something else by the clip's length:
658	
659	| Template | What follows the clip's length |
660	| --- | --- |
661	| Counter | Reaches its final number about 70 % of the way through. |
662	| Progress bar | Reaches its value about 60 % of the way through. |
663	| Subscribe button | The first click lands 40 % of the way through. |
664	
665	[Countdown](#countdown) and [News ticker](#news-ticker) run in real time whatever the clip's length. To fix a graphic's length so it no longer follows the clip, see [The graphic's own timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/#the-graphics-own-timeline).

667	## Titles & Text
668	
669	### Chapter card
670	
671	A card with a large outlined chapter number, a kicker beside it, an accent rule drawing across and the title rising into view.
672	
673	| Property | What it does | Default |
674	| --- | --- | --- |
675	| **number** | The chapter number, 0 to 99, always shown as two digits. | 1 |
676	| **kicker** | The small text beside the number. It wraps, shrinking to stay within three lines, down to a smallest size. | CHAPTER |
677	| **title** | The title under the rule, fitted to the width. | Getting started |
678	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#0b0b10` |
679	| **accent** | The number's outline and the rule. | `#ff5a36` |
680	
681	### Kinetic type
682	
683	A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, on a near-black card. Every fifth word, counting from the fourth, takes the accent colour.
684	
685	| Property | What it does | Default |
686	| --- | --- | --- |
687	| **text** | The sentence. | Make something people want to watch twice, then cut it in half |
688	| **stagger** | Frames between one word and the next, 1 to 30. | 4 |
689	| **color** | Most of the words. | `#ffffff` |
690	| **accent** | The fourth word, the ninth, the fourteenth and so on. | `#ffd60a` |
691	
692	The sentence wraps at 80 % of the canvas's width, at one fixed size, and centres on the frame. A long one can run off the top and bottom, so split it across two clips. The card's colour isn't a property.
693	
694	### Logo reveal
695	
696	A card on which an accent bar sweeps across, revealing your logo or a text mark. The bar then settles into a short rule, and a tagline fades up under it.
697	
698	| Property | What it does | Default |
699	| --- | --- | --- |
700	| **logo** | A picture to reveal. **None** draws the **mark** instead. | None |
701	| **mark** | The text to reveal when there's no picture, fitted to the width. | FRAME JOB |
702	| **tagline** | The line under the rule. Leave it empty for none. | Edit at the speed of thought |
703	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#0b0b10` |
704	| **accent** | The bar and the rule. | `#ff5a36` |

content.content:
The **logo** pop-up lists the pictures added to the project's graphics, so add yours first with **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). The picture keeps its proportions inside a box half the width of the title-safe area.
### Lower third
A name and a subtitle that slide in from the left and fade out, on a dark bar with an accent edge.
The box grows to fit the longer line, and the text isn't shrunk to fit. A long name at a large **size** can run off the frame.
### News ticker
A band along the foot of the frame with a headline box at its left and items crawling right to left, with an accent dot between them. Type the items in one field, separated by a vertical bar (`|`). They repeat for as long as the clip runs.
### Quote card
A card with a large quote mark, the quote's lines fading up in turn, and a short rule and the attribution sliding in.
The quote shrinks and wraps to fit the frame. It wraps by itself, so line breaks you type are treated as spaces.
### Title card
A title fitted to the frame with a kicker above it, over a diagonal two-colour gradient. The text fades in and rises, then fades out over the last 18 frames, and the gradient stays.
## Screencast
### Arrow highlight
Points at something on a screen recording: a rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail.
With `box` the label sits under the box, or above it when there's no room. With `arrow` the arrow points at the spot itself and the two box sizes do nothing. The box, arrow and label are always kept inside the title-safe area, so a spot near the edge is moved in.
### Callout
A circle that draws itself round a spot, with an arrow and a label.
The arrow always comes from the lower left, and nothing keeps it on the frame. Near the left or bottom edge the arrow and label run off, so use [Arrow highlight](#arrow-highlight) there.
### Keyboard keys
A shortcut drawn as keycaps that pop in one after another and are then pressed in turn, with a label under them.
The names in **keys** can be in any case:
A long row of keys shrinks to fit the frame. A clip needs at least 25 frames plus 10 for each key to press them all before its exit, so a shortcut of seven or more keys wants longer than the default 90 frames.
[Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) places clips drawn by this template for you, from the shortcuts in a screen recording.
### Step badge
A numbered accent circle popping in at a corner, with a label panel wiping out from behind it.
### Window frame
A browser or app window's frame to sit over a screen recording: a title bar with three dots, a title or an address field, and a rounded outline. The inside stays clear.
Put the recording on a track below the frame, then use the [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) to fit it inside the outline.
The shadow is only as wide as the room around the frame, so it thins out as **scale** nears 1.
## Social & YouTube
### End screen
A card laid out for a video's end screen: a title, two 16:9 spaces and a subscribe circle. On a landscape or square canvas the two spaces sit side by side with the circle centred under them. On a portrait canvas they're a column.
The spaces are placeholders drawn into the picture, for the video elements you add on the platform when you publish. They don't link to anything.
### Handle tag
An accent tile holding a glyph, with a pill showing your @handle expanding from behind it, at a corner.
### Social popup
A notification card rising in at a corner, with a generic avatar and a handle. Its heart, speech bubble or share arrow pops as the count ticks up by one.
### Subscribe button
A button that a cursor glides to and clicks. It turns grey with a check and its done label, then a bell pops in beside it and rings after a second click.
## Data & Time
The three charts read their data from text fields, with entries separated by commas:
- Values and labels pair up by position, and a value with no label has a blank one.
- An entry that isn't a number is dropped, so the values after it line up one label earlier.
- An empty entry, such as a comma at the end, counts as 0.
### Bar chart
Bars growing one after another on a dark card, each with its figure above it and its label below, under a title.
The tallest bar sets the scale, and the figures are rounded to whole numbers. The card's colour isn't a property.
### Countdown
A timer counting down or up, one step a second, inside a ring that empties or fills. The digits pulse on each tick, and the circle flashes in the accent colour at the end.
The count runs in real seconds whatever the frame rate, so the clip's length decides how far it gets. The default 330 frames is 11 seconds at 30 fps, which fits a ten-second count and the exit. At 60 fps that clip is 5.5 seconds, so lengthen it. For any longer count, lengthen the clip to the count plus a second.
With **from** and **to** equal there's nothing to count: the number stands in a full ring and nothing flashes.
### Counter
A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label under it. It starts fast and slows into its final number, then holds.
The number shows no decimals, and it isn't shrunk to fit, so a very long one can run past the edges.
### Donut chart
Slices sweeping round a donut on a dark card, with the first slice's share counting up in the centre above its label, and a legend with each share. The legend sits beside the donut on a landscape or square canvas, and below it on a portrait one.
The other slices take colours from a fixed set of six, in order, repeating after the sixth. The shares are rounded to whole percentages, so they may not add up to exactly 100. The card's colour isn't a property.
### Gauge
A 270° dial with ticks, whose accent arc and needle swing to a value while the figure counts up.
A whole **value** counts in whole numbers, and any other shows one decimal place.
### Line chart
A line drawn on through its points on a dark card, a dot popping at each one, with the last value called out in a pill.
The scale runs from 0, or from the lowest value if that's negative, up to the highest. A single value draws one dot and no line. The card's colour isn't a property.
### Progress bar
A labelled bar on a dark plate, filling to a percentage with the figure counting, and a shine sweeping across it once it has filled.
## Any canvas shape
Templates size themselves by the shorter side of the size they draw at, which is the canvas's unless you change it, so nothing grows too large on a tall project.
Seventeen of them are laid out for all three shapes. Everything they draw stays inside the title-safe area, the frame less 5 % on every side, at 1920 × 1080, 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. Their entrances are a spring, a wipe or a fade, and never a move in from outside the frame. Long text is fitted or wrapped to stay inside, down to a smallest size for each text, so a paragraph typed where a title belongs can still run over.
The other six are Bar chart, Callout, Counter, Kinetic type, Lower third and Title card. They don't keep to the title-safe area, and a left-aligned Lower third enters from beyond the frame's left edge. Once settled, with their default text, their words sit at least 24 pixels inside a 1080 × 1920 frame. Only Title card fits its title and Kinetic type wraps its text, so check your own words on a tall canvas. [Safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) shows the title-safe guide in the preview.
A square canvas takes the landscape layout.
## Templates end clean
The same seventeen each have an accent colour and leave in about their last 15 frames, so the last frame is bare. An overlay ends clear, and a card ends on its background alone. A card's background never animates: only what's on it moves or fades.
The other six end their own way:
## Template fonts and glyphs
Templates draw only with fonts that come with Frame Job, so a project looks the same on any Mac. The font isn't a property. To change it, [edit the graphic's code](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
Every symbol is a generic shape drawn by the template, never a brand's artwork: the keycap symbols, the heart, the bell, the play triangle and the glyphs in Handle tag. None of them is a platform's own logo.
## Good to know
- Each insert copies the template into the project under a name not yet in use, such as `lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`. Undo takes the clip away, and the copy stays until you [delete it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
- Your copy is yours to change, and it stays as it was when you inserted it. [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) covers the one exception.
- Most properties can [change over time with an action](/graphics/animate-properties/). These keep one value for the whole clip: **number** in Chapter card and Step badge, **values** and **labels** in Donut chart and Line chart, **keys** in Keyboard keys, **items** in News ticker and **count** in Social popup.
## With an agent
[`list_graphics`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#list_graphics) lists the templates by category, as the sheet does. [`insert_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#insert_graphic) places one at the playhead: give it the name `list_graphics` shows, such as `arrow-highlight`, with `from` set to `template`. The reply names the project's copy, which may be `arrow-highlight-2`. To fill in the properties afterwards, use [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic), with the names in the tables above. See [Tools: g
## Related
- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)

1	---
2	title: "Insert a graphic"
3	description: "Pick a bundled template, a graphic already in your project or a file of your own, preview it, and place it at the playhead."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	**Insert ▸ Graphic…** is where you put a motion graphic on the timeline. You can pick one of the 23 bundled templates, a graphic already in your project, or a file of your own, and watch it play before you place it.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
14	  tools={['list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'render_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
15	/>
16	
17	<Shot
18	  name="15e-graphic-browser-sheet.sheet"
19	  alt="The Insert Graphic sheet. On the left, the categories This Project, Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text. In the middle, the list of graphics, with Lower third chosen. On the right, the lower third plays over a checkerboard, with its title and the line A name and a subtitle sliding in on a bar under it. The bottom bar has Export… and From File… at the left, and Cancel and Insert at the right."
20	/>
21	
22	## Insert a graphic
23	
24	<Steps>
25	
26	1. Move the playhead to where the graphic should start.
27	
28	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**. The item has no keyboard shortcut, and it's dimmed until the project's window is open.
29	
30	3. Choose a category on the left, then a graphic in the middle. The preview on the right plays it.
31	
32	4. Choose **Insert**, press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or double-click the graphic in the list.
33	
34	</Steps>
35	
36	Frame Job places the clip, selects it and closes the sheet. The inspector's **Clip** tab shows the new clip on its [**Graphic** sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/), ready for you to fill in.
37	
38	Placing the clip is one undo step, **Insert Graphic**. If the graphic was a template, Frame Job first copied it into your project, and undo leaves that file where it is. See [Templates are copied in](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#templates-are-copied-in).
39	
40	**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and changes nothing.
41	
42	## The Insert Graphic sheet
43	
44	The sheet has three panes, over a message line. The bottom bar has **Export…** and **From File…** at the left, and **Cancel** and **Insert** at the right. It opens on the first category's first graphic.
45	
46	**Insert** is dimmed when no graphic is chosen. **Export…** saves the chosen graphic to give to someone else, and it's dimmed for a module that doesn't compile and while another export is running: see [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
47	
48	### Categories
49	
50	The left list files the graphics by category. **This Project** comes first when your project holds a module, then the bundled categories in alphabetical order:
51	
52	- **Data & Time**
53	- **Screencast**
54	- **Social & YouTube**
55	- **Titles & Text**
56	
57	**This Project** lists every module in the project's `graphics` folder. A module of your own always appears there, whatever category it [names for itself](/graphics/write-a-module/), and never in a bundled category. [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) lists what's in each category.
58	
59	The sheet reads what's in your project when it opens. A module you add while it's open appears the next time you open it.
60	
61	### The graphics list
62	
63	The middle list shows the chosen category's graphics, sorted by title. A title comes from the module's own name for itself. Without one, Frame Job makes a title from the file name, so `lower-third` becomes Lower Third.
64	
65	When two graphics under **This Project** share a title, each shows its module name as well, as in "Lower third — lower-third-2".
66	
67	A module that [doesn't compile](#a-module-that-doesnt-compile) is still listed, in grey. Choose it and the preview shows its red error card, so you can find out why it won't insert.
68	
69	### The looping preview
70	
71	The chosen graphic plays on a loop over a checkerboard, so you can see what's transparent. The preview has your project's canvas shape, and the graphic's title and a one-line description sit under it. A module of your own gets that line from [its own description](/graphics/write-a-module/). Hold the pointer over a description that's cut off to read all of it.
72	
73	The preview uses the graphic's default properties, at the project's frame rate. A slow graphic skips frames rather than falling behind. A module that fails shows its red error card here.
74	
75	## Insert from This Project
76	
77	Choosing a graphic under **This Project** places another clip drawn by that module, as it is. Nothing is copied, so this is how you use one graphic on several clips. Each clip keeps its own property values, but editing the module changes every clip it draws. See [Clips sharing one module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#clips-sharing-one-module).
78	
79	## Insert from a file
80	
81	<Steps>
82	
83	1. Choose **From File…**. The sheet closes and a file panel opens.
84	
85	2. Choose a `.js` module, or a `.fjgraphic` package.
86	
87	</Steps>
88	
89	Frame Job copies a `.js` file into the project under a [new name](#how-the-module-is-named) and places a clip drawn by it, as **Insert** does. The file must be UTF-8 text. If it isn't, Frame Job says so and copies nothing.
90	
91	A `.fjgraphic` package doesn't go straight in. Frame Job shows you what's in it and asks first: see [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
92	
93	### How the module is named
94	
95	The module is named after the file you chose, changed as needed to make a valid [module name](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#module-names) that isn't taken:
96	
97	1. The name is lowercased.
98	2. Each run of anything other than a to z and 0 to 9 becomes one `-`.
99	3. Dashes are trimmed from the ends.
100	4. The result is cut to 60 characters. If nothing is left, the name is `graphic`.
101	5. If that name is taken, it gets `-2`, `-3` and so on.
102	
103	So `My Title.js` becomes `my-title`, and `My Counter (v2).js` becomes `my-counter-v2`.
104	
105	## Where it lands
106	
107	A new graphic starts at the playhead, on the front track (the top lane) if there's room for it. If there isn't, it goes on a new track above everything. [Adding a text clip](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) follows the same rule.
108	
109	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the clip goes on the nest's front track, or on a new track inside the nest.
110	
111	## Default length and size
112	
113	A module can give its own length and size. Otherwise the clip is 5 seconds long and the size of the canvas.
114	
115	A module gives its length in frames, counted at the project's frame rate, so a 150-frame graphic lasts 5 seconds at 30 fps and 2.5 seconds at 60 fps. [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) lists each template's length. You can change the length and size afterwards: see [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
116	
117	A graphic bigger than the canvas is scaled down to fit when **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/), as a shape is. It still draws at its own size.
118	
119	Frame Job won't place a clip when the module's length isn't a whole number of at least 1 frame, or its width or height isn't a whole number from 1 to 8192. The message names the value that's wrong. A module that gives no size of its own can't be placed on a canvas wider or taller than 8192 pixels.
120	
121	## A module that doesn't compile
122	
123	A module that doesn't compile has an error in its code that stops Frame Job running it. No clip is placed, and Frame Job tells you the first error, and the line it's on when it knows:
124	
125	> `graphics/<name>.js does not compile: <message> (line N)`
126	
127	From the sheet, Frame Job beeps, the message appears under the lists and the sheet stays open. **From File…** shows it in an alert.
128	
129	A copy Frame Job made along the way stays in your project, whether it came from a template or a file. You'll find it in grey under **This Project**. Fix it and insert it from there, or remove it with [**File ▸ Delete Graphic…**](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
130	
131	A message about a length or size that's out of range appears in the same places.
132	
133	## On the timeline
134	
135	A graphic clip is teal and has no thumbnails. Its strip shows a `{}` symbol and reads **Graphic**, until you [give it a name](/timeline/names-and-labels/). When it's selected, the [timeline bar](/getting-started/editor-window/#timeline-bar) and the inspector's clip header give its kind as "graphic".
136	
137	## With an agent
138	
139	An agent can list what the sheet offers with [`list_graphics`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#list_graphics) and insert a graphic at the playhead with [`insert_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#insert_graphic), as you can. It can also do two things the sheet can't: draw chosen frames of a module to a picture without placing a clip, with [`render_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#render_graphic), and place a clip on the track and at the time it chooses, with its own length, size and property values, with [`add_graphic_clip`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#add_graphic_clip). See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/).
140	
141	## Related
142	
143	- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
144	- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
145	- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
146	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
147	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
148	- [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/)
149	---
150	title: Share a graphic
151	description: Save a graphic as a .fjgraphic file with the fonts and pictures it uses, and bring one into another project.
152	---
153	
154	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
155	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
156	
157	A `.fjgraphic` file, called a package on this page, carries one graphic with the fonts and pictures it uses, so you can move it to another project or give it to someone else with Frame Job. Finder calls the file a Frame Job Graphic.
158	
159	<AtAGlance
160	  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
161	  where={['Export… and From File… in the Insert Graphic sheet', 'A .fjgraphic opened from the Finder']}
162	  tools={['export_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
163	/>
164	
165	## Export a graphic
166	
167	<Steps>
168	
169	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…** and pick the graphic in the Insert Graphic sheet. It can be a bundled template or one from **This Project**.
170	
171	2. Choose **Export…**. It's dimmed when the chosen graphic doesn't compile, and while another export is running.
172	
173	3. A save panel slides down over the sheet, with the file already named after the module, such as `lower-third.fjgraphic`. Choose where to put it and save.
174	
175	</Steps>
176	
177	The Insert Graphic sheet stays open. The line under its lists says `Exporting <title>…`, then `Exported <title> to <file>:` followed by the files the package holds, or says why it couldn't.
178	
179	Saving over an existing file replaces it whole. If the export fails, the file already there is left as it was.
180	
181	Exporting changes nothing in the project and isn't an undo step.
182	
183	## What a package packs
184	
185	A package holds the [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules), which is the script that draws the graphic, and only the project fonts and pictures the graphic uses. To find those, Frame Job draws the graphic and packs what it saw used:
186	
187	- Every frame with the default properties. A graphic longer than 900 frames has 900 frames spread evenly over it.
188	- Then each other choice of each [Enum](/graphics/properties/#enum) property and the other value of each [Boolean](/graphics/properties/#boolean) property, one at a time, over up to 30 frames each. It tries at most 32 of these.
189	
190	A font is packed when the graphic drew or measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font lacks. A picture is packed when the graphic's `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are never packed, because every copy of Frame Job has them, so a bundled template's package holds its module and nothing else.
191	
192	A frame that fails to draw is skipped.
193	
194	:::caution
195	[String](/graphics/properties/#string) and [Asset](/graphics/properties/#asset) properties are only tried at their defaults. A font or picture the graphic reaches only through another value, such as a different title or another picture, isn't packed. Read the file list in the message line after an export, and if something's missing, make it that property's default in the module and export again.
196	:::
197	
198	## The .fjgraphic file
199	
200	A package is a zip with nothing compressed. It holds `manifest.json`, the module, and the `fonts/` and `assets/` folders. The manifest gives the package's format, the module, its title, category and description, the Frame Job version that wrote it, and each file's path, name, size and SHA-256.
201	
202	Exporting the same graphic twice with the same version of Frame Job gives byte-identical files.
203	
204	A file name a zip path can't hold is stored under a tidied name. That covers a `:` or `\`, a control character and a leading `.`, so `a:b.ttf` is stored as `a-b.ttf`. The manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and `asset(name)` still finds its picture.
205	
206	A package can hold at most about 4 GiB and 65,535 files.
207	
208	## Open from the Finder
209	
210	Frame Job is the app macOS uses for these files. Double-click a `.fjgraphic`, open it with **Open With**, drop it on Frame Job's Dock icon, or open it from a browser's downloads. Frame Job [checks the package](#package-checks), then puts up the [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet).
211	
212	The package goes into the front project, the one whose window is in front. With no project open, it goes into a new untitled project. A package that fails its checks before the sheet appears shows an alert and opens no project.
213	
214	If Frame Job wasn't running, it opens first and the package waits until any projects it reopens are back, so it lands once, in one project, with no Welcome window.
215	
216	**File ▸ Open…** doesn't list `.fjgraphic` files, and there's no menu item for importing one.
217	
218	## Import with From File…
219	
220	<Steps>
221	
222	1. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**. The Insert Graphic sheet closes and a file panel opens.
223	
224	2. Choose a `.fjgraphic`. The [Import Graphic sheet](#the-import-graphic-sheet) appears for that same project.
225	
226	</Steps>
227	
228	The panel also takes a `.js` module, which goes straight onto the timeline. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
229	
230	## The Import Graphic sheet
231	
232	Before anything is copied, the sheet shows the graphic's title and description, then what will happen to each file:
233	
234	| Line | What it can read |
235	| --- | --- |
236	| Module | `Module: lower-third`, `Module: lower-third (already in this project)`, or `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)` |
237	| Fonts | The font files, each plain, marked `(already here)`, or marked `(as Inter-2.ttf)`. With none, `Fonts: none`. |
238	| Pictures | The picture files, each plain or marked `(already here)`. With none, `Pictures: none`. |
239	
240	Under them it says "Importing copies these files into this project's graphics. It is not an Undo step."
241	
242	Choose **Import** to copy the files, or **Cancel** to copy nothing.
243	
244	If the project's graphics folder changed while the sheet was up and the import can't go ahead, Frame Job beeps, the sheet stays open and it says why.
245	
246	## Name clashes
247	
248	An import never replaces a file. Each file keeps the name the package gives it, unless that name is taken:
249	
250	| The project already has | What happens |
251	| --- | --- |
252	| A file of that name with the same contents | It's used as it is, and the sheet says "already here", or "already in this project" for the module. |
253	| A different module of that name | The module is copied under a new name with `-2`, `-3` and so on: `Module: lower-third-2 (lower-third is taken)`. |
254	| A different font of that name | The font is copied under a new name, such as `as Inter-2.ttf`. A font is found by its family, so its file name changes nothing. |
255	| A different picture of that name | The import stops, because the module asks for its pictures by name. An alert says so. Rename or remove the project's file and import again. |
256	
257	A name that differs only in case counts as taken. A module name also counts as taken while any clip still uses it, even when its file is gone.
258	
259	To find the project's pictures, see [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
260	
261	## After an import
262	
263	**Import** copies the files into the project's graphics folder and opens the Insert Graphic sheet on **This Project** with the graphic chosen, ready to insert. The line under the lists says what happened:
264	
265	`Imported Lower third as lower-third. Added: lower-third.js, fonts/Inter.ttf. Already here: assets/logo.png.`
266	
267	An import only copies files. It places no clip, so choose **Insert** when you want one on the timeline.
268	
269	Importing isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited. An untitled project keeps the files when it's first saved. If a copy fails part-way, what it had copied is removed.
270	
271	## Package checks
272	
273	Frame Job checks a package before it copies anything. If a check fails, nothing is copied, and the message reads `<file> cannot be imported:` followed by the reason.
274	
275	| What's wrong | What the reason says |
276	| --- | --- |
277	| The file is empty | `it is empty (0 bytes)` |
278	| It isn't a zip, or it's damaged | For example `the package is not a zip: no end of central directory record` |
279	| It was compressed, for example by zipping it again | `<entry> is compressed (method 8); a .fjgraphic holds stored entries only` |
280	| It was changed after it was written | The entry that differs from the manifest by path, size or SHA-256, such as `<entry> is 2048 bytes, but the manifest says 1024` |
281	| A newer Frame Job wrote it | `the package is format 2; this Frame Job reads format 1 — a newer Frame Job wrote it` |
282	| A font is bad | `the font "<name>" is not a .ttf or .otf file`, or why it doesn't load |
283	| A picture is bad | `the picture "<name>"` and why: it isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file, its name can't be used, or it's empty |
284	
285	A module that doesn't compile passes these checks and is imported. It's listed on **This Project** with **Export…** dimmed, and **Insert** places nothing and shows the first error. Fix it the way you'd fix any module. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
286	
287	## With an agent
288	
289	[`export_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#export_graphic) is **Export…**, writing to a path instead of through a save panel, and it also says how many frames it drew and how many failed. It writes nothing for an unknown graphic, a module that doesn't compile or a folder that doesn't exist. The Assistant asks you before it runs, because it can replace a file.
290	
291	[`import_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#import_graphic) is **Import** without the sheet, so nothing asks first. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

317	## The Graphic sub-tab
318	
319	A graphic clip's sub-tabs are **Graphic**, **Picture** and **Clip**, in that order. **Graphic** appears only when every selected clip is a graphic clip, so any other kind of clip in the selection removes it.
320	
321	| Section | What it's for | Summary when collapsed | Starts | Shows |
322	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
323	| [Source](#source) | What draws the clip, and what the module reports about it | The error or warning count, or the module's display name | Collapsed | Always |
324	| [Properties](/graphics/properties/) | What the graphic shows | The number of properties | Open | When every selected clip is drawn by one module |
325	| [Size](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's width and height | `W × H` | Collapsed | Always |
326	| [Timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | The graphic's own timeline | Its length | Collapsed | With one clip selected |
327	
328	There's no **Color** sub-tab. To grade a graphic, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above it.
329	
330	## The Picture sub-tab
331	
332	A graphic has the same layer settings as other clips, so you can move, scale and fade it: [Transform](/canvas/transform/) (position, scale, rotation and opacity), [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/), [Shadow](/effects/shadow/), [Filters](/effects/filters/), [Reflection](/effects/reflection/), [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) and [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
333	
334	It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, which are for clips drawn from media.
335	
336	## The Clip sub-tab
337	
338	**Clip** has the clip's [Timing](/editing/timing-section/) when one clip is selected, [Transition](/motion/transition-settings/) when the clip overlaps the one before it, and [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
339	
340	There's no Speed section. A graphic has no speed control or speed ramp, because its timing comes from the module and its [Length](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
341	
342	## Source
343	
344	Source says what draws the clip. Its summary, when collapsed, is `1 error` or `2 warnings` if there's anything to report, and otherwise the module's display name.
345	
346	### Name, File and Revision
347	
348	| Row | What it shows |
349	| --- | --- |
350	| **Name** | The module's display name, or its file name when it has none |
351	| **File** | The module's file, `<name>.js` |
352	| **Revision** | The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the file's text, which change whenever the text does, or `missing` when the file is gone |
353	
354	### Open in Editor
355	
356	**Open in Editor** opens the module in the app your Mac uses for `.js` files. Save there and the preview redraws within a moment. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
357	
358	### Reveal in Finder
359	
360	**Reveal in Finder** shows the module's file in a Finder window.
361	
362	Below these two, **Duplicate as New Graphic…** makes a copy of the module for the selected clips. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
363	
364	## Diagnostics
365	
366	Under the buttons, Source lists what the module says about the clip, under a heading for each stage:
367	
368	- **Compiling the module** appears when there's something to report: the compile error, or any warnings the module gave as it loaded.
369	- **No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame** means that frame drew cleanly. **Checked at the clip's first frame** is followed by what that frame reported. Neither appears when the module didn't compile.
370	
371	The first frame is drawn at the clip's own size, so a missing font, a picture that isn't in the project or a size mismatch shows here. With several clips of one module selected, the check uses the first of them.
372	
373	Each row reads `line L, column C — message`, `line L — message` when it has no column, or the message alone when it has no place in the file. An error is in the stronger text colour and a warning is muted.
374	
375	While you drag a control, the list holds still. It updates when you let go.
376	
377	### Open a diagnostic
378	
379	Click a diagnostic, or its **Open** button, to open the module in your editor. This opens the file, not the line, so note the line number first.
380	
381	### In the graphics folder
382	
383	**In the graphics folder** lists what Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch when it scanned the project's graphics folder:
384	
385	- A module or picture with a bad name.
386	- An empty picture.
387	- A font that doesn't load.
388	- A file that couldn't be watched.
389	
390	Each row has a **Reveal** button, and clicking it or the row shows the graphics folder in Finder, not the file. These rows count as warnings in the section's summary.
391	
392	## A missing module
393	
394	When the module's file is gone, **Open in Editor**, **Reveal in Finder** and **Duplicate as New Graphic…** are dimmed, **Revision** reads `missing`, and Source shows the error `No module named "<name>" in graphics/`.
395	
396	If Frame Job kept an earlier version, you can [restore it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
397	
398	## Several modules selected
399	
400	When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, Source starts open and its summary counts them, such as `2 modules`. It names them and says:
401	
402	> Drawn by different modules: lower-third, title-card
403	>
404	> Select one module's clips to edit its properties.
405	
406	The rows, buttons and diagnostics are gone until you do. **Size** stays editable, because it doesn't depend on the module. **Properties** needs one module and **Timeline** needs one clip.
407	
408	## Switching clips to another module
409	
410	The inspector can't point clips at a different module that already exists. **Duplicate as New Graphic…** only switches them to a new copy.
411	
412	To move clips to an existing module, delete them and [insert that module](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) again. An agent can do it in one step: [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic) with the clips and the new module's `name` draws them from that module, which must be in the project's graphics folder and compile.

442	## Property rows
443	
444	Properties shows one row for each property the module defines, in the module's own order. A row's label is the one the module gives it, or the property's key when it gives none, and resting the pointer on the row shows the module's help text. The section starts open, and its summary counts the rows, such as `6 properties`.
445	
446	Every row is a normal inspector row. A change is one undo step, and you can right-click a row's label to reset it. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
447	
448	If there are no rows, the section says why:
449	
450	| It says | What it means |
451	| --- | --- |
452	| "The module declares no properties." | The graphic has nothing to set. |
453	| "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." | The module is missing or doesn't compile, so Frame Job can't read its properties until it's fixed. See [Diagnostics](/graphics/graphic-tab/#diagnostics). The clip's values are kept and listed as [leftover values](#leftover-values). |
454	
455	A module gives each property one of six types, and the type sets the control. The headings below use the names a module uses.
456	
457	### Number
458	
459	A value field, with a slider beside it when the module gives both a minimum and a maximum. A number past the range is held to the end of the range.
460	
461	The field shows two decimals when the module's step is below 1. With no step, it shows two decimals when the default or a bound has a fraction. Otherwise it shows whole numbers.
462	
463	### String
464	
465	Text, in a one-line field the width of the inspector. Long text scrolls inside it.
466	
467	When the module marks the property as multi-line, it's a text area instead: <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line.
468	
469	A property holds at most 4,096 characters.
470	
471	### Boolean
472	
473	A checkbox, for something that's either on or off.
474	
475	### Enum
476	
477	A pop-up, for a choice from a fixed list. A module offers 1 to 32 options.
478	
479	### Color
480	
481	A colour swatch. Click it to open the macOS colour panel. A colour you can see through keeps its opacity. Frame Job stores the colour as `#rrggbb`, or as `#rrggbbaa` when it isn't fully opaque.
482	
483	### Asset
484	
485	A pop-up of pictures. It lists **None**, then every picture in the project's graphics, then any picture name that's referred to but missing from the folder. A missing name comes from the selected clips, the selected action's end or the module's default, so a missing picture still shows by name.
486	
487	**None** gives the module no picture, even when it has a default one.
488	
489	To add a picture to the list, choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…** first. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
490	
491	## Reset
492	
493	A **Reset** button appears on the section's header while a row differs from the module's default. Click it to clear every value stored on the selected clips, so the module draws its own defaults. It's one undo step, named **Reset Graphic Properties**.
494	
495	To put back one row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
496	
497	While an action is selected, the rows edit the action's end, not the clip, except a property the module marks `animate: false`. The header has no **Reset** then. It shows **Clear** once the action sets one of the rows, and right-clicking a row offers **Set end value to default**. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
498	
499	## Values at the default
500	
501	With no action selected, setting a value back to the module's default clears it from the clip. The clip then follows the module's default if that changes later.
502	
503	A colour counts as the default when its channels match, however the module spelled it.
504	
505	The exception is a property an action on the clip animates. There, Frame Job keeps the default as a stored value, so the animation keeps its start.
506	
507	## Editing several clips
508	
509	With several clips of one module selected, a change to a row applies to all of them, as one undo step. A row whose clips disagree shows the first clip's value with a **mixed** badge. See [Edit several clips at once](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
510	
511	Properties appears only when all the selected clips share one module. Clips of different modules can't be edited together. An agent can't set their properties in one go either, unless the same call moves them all to one module. See [Several modules selected](/graphics/graphic-tab/#several-modules-selected).
512	
513	<a id="stale-values"></a>
514	
515	## Leftover values
516	
517	A clip can hold a value for a property the module no longer has, for example after you rename a property in the module. The value stays, listed below the rows with its key dimmed, its value beside it, and **⌫** to remove it.
518	
519	The clip still draws. The value is passed to the module, and Source shows the warning `props.<key> is not in the schema; it is passed through`.
520	
521	**⌫** removes the value from every selected clip, as one undo step named **Remove Graphic Property**.
522	
523	With no compiled module, every stored value is listed this way. An action's end has leftover rows of its own, marked as the action's. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
524	
525	## Good to know
526	
527	A stored value that no longer suits its property, such as a choice the module has dropped from an [Enum](#enum), isn't listed as a leftover. The clip draws the module's default, and Source shows a warning naming the property.
528	
529	## With an agent
530	
531	[`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic) changes the same values, on any number of clips of one module, as one undo step. Setting a property to `null` clears it from the clips, except a property an action on the clip animates, which is set to the module's default.

553	## Width and Height
554	
555	**Width** and **Height** are the size the graphic draws at, in whole pixels from 1 to 8192 a side. The graphic's code lays itself out at that size, so text and shapes stay sharp.
556	
557	The **Size** section starts collapsed, and its header shows the size, for example `1920 × 1080`. With several graphic clips selected, a change applies to all of them, and a row shows mixed when they differ.
558	
559	A new graphic takes the size its [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), the code that draws it, asks for, or the canvas's size if it doesn't ask.
560	
561	The graphic is drawn at this size and then placed on the canvas like any other layer. Scaling the clip in the [Picture](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab scales that finished picture. To make a graphic bigger and keep it crisp, raise **Width** and **Height** rather than the scale.
562	
563	Changing the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) never changes a graphic's size. [Make Vertical Version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) is the one exception.
564	
565	## Fit to Canvas
566	
567	**Fit to Canvas** in the **Size** section sets the size to the canvas's, then centres the clip at scale 1. It works on every selected graphic clip, as one undo step called Fit Graphic to Canvas.
568	
569	A graphic can't be larger than 8192 pixels a side, so on a bigger canvas Frame Job tells you why and leaves the clip as it was.
570	
571	## The graphic's own timeline
572	
573	A graphic counts its own frames from its first frame, separately from the project's timeline. The **Timeline** section shows where the clip sits on that count. It appears only when one clip is selected, it starts collapsed, and its header shows the length.
574	
575	| Row | What it shows | What you can do |
576	| --- | --- | --- |
577	| **In** | The graphic frame the clip's first frame shows. | Nothing directly. Trimming the front, rolling the cut before the clip and splitting all move it. |
578	| **Length** | How long the graphic's own timeline runs. | Type a timecode to pin it. |
579	| **Follow Clip** | Whether the graphic's timeline ends when the clip ends. | Tick or untick it. |
580	
581	### Follow Clip
582	
583	**Follow Clip** is on for a new clip. The graphic's timeline ends with the clip, so when you lengthen the clip its outro moves to the new end. Most graphics want this.
584	
585	Unticking **Follow Clip** pins **Length** at its current value. Ticking it again hands the length back to the clip.
586	
587	### Length
588	
589	Typing in **Length** pins it, which unticks **Follow Clip**, and is one undo step called Graphic Length. A pinned graphic keeps its pace however long the clip gets, so the animation doesn't stretch and its outro stays at the same point.
590	
591	The value snaps to a frame and can't be less than one frame. Typing the value the field already shows changes nothing, so untick **Follow Clip** to pin the length as it stands.
592	
593	### Length shorter or longer than the clip
594	
595	When **Length** is pinned shorter than the clip, the graphic keeps counting frames past it, but its progress stays at the end. What you see depends on how the graphic is written:
596	
597	- An animation driven by progress holds its end state.
598	- An animation driven by frame numbers keeps going.
599	
600	When **Length** is pinned longer than the clip, the clip ends before the graphic's timeline does, so a late outro never plays.
601	
602	## Trim a graphic like footage
603	
604	Trimming a graphic clip cuts into its animation, as trimming a video cuts into its footage. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) and [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) work as they do on any clip.
605	
606	| Edit | What happens |
607	| --- | --- |
608	| Trim the start, or roll the cut before the clip | **In** moves, so the animation starts further in. **Length** stays the same, so the outro keeps its timing. |
609	| Trim the end, **Follow Clip** on | The graphic's timeline ends at the clip's new end. |
610	| Trim the end, **Length** pinned | **Length** doesn't change. Shortening the clip can cut off the outro. |
611	| Drag the start earlier | A graphic has no source to run out of, so the start can go back as far as the track allows. **In** moves back and stops at 0. |
612	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) the clip | The second half's **In** moves, so it carries on where the first half left off. Both halves pin **Length** to the original's, which unticks **Follow Clip** on both and keeps the outro at the same point. |
613	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | The clip stretches or squeezes like a title. A pinned **Length** stays as it was. |
614	
615	## Good to know
616	
617	- Actions can't animate size or timing. With an action selected, the **Size** and **Timeline** sections show ⊘ and always change the clip. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
618	- Adding a [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) that gives a graphic clip extra frames at its head moves **In** back by the same amount, so the picture stays in step. Where **In** is shorter than the extension it stops at 0, and the graphic's first frame lands on the clip's new first frame.
619	- Changing the [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) moves a graphic's own timeline onto the new frames. **In** and a pinned **Length** snap to the nearest frame. A graphic that counts in seconds keeps its pace, and one that counts frames runs faster at a higher rate.
620	
621	## With an agent
622	
623	An agent sets the size and the length with [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic), and can give a size to [`add_graphic_clip`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#add_graphic_clip) as it places the clip. A `length` of null is **Follow Clip**. To do what **Fit to Canvas** does, it sets the size with `set_graphic`, then the position and scale with [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/#set_video).
624	
625	No tool sets **In** directly. It moves with [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start), [`roll`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#roll) and splits, as it does in the app. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic).
626

633	---
634	title: "Graphics in a vertical version"
635	description: How Make Vertical Version re-sizes and re-lays your graphics for a tall or square canvas, which older template copies it updates, and which modules it names for you to check.
636	---
637	
638	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
639	
640	[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) has to turn a wide layout into a tall or square one, and graphics can lay themselves out again where footage can't. This page says what happens to each graphic, and which ones you might want to look at afterwards.
641	
642	<AtAGlance
643	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
644	  tools="make_vertical_version"
645	/>
646	
647	## Canvas-sized graphics
648	
649	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, each side, is re-sized to the new canvas, so its [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), the code that draws it, lays it out again on the new frame. This is usually a full-frame lower third or title card. A 1920 × 1080 graphic on a 1920 × 1080 canvas becomes 1080 × 1920 for 9:16.
650	
651	Its position shrinks and stretches with the two sides of the canvas, and so do the positions its [actions](/graphics/animate-properties/) move it to. Its scale stays as it was, because the graphic is the canvas's size again.
652	
653	This is the one change of canvas that changes a graphic's size. Everywhere else, [Width and Height](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height) stay as you set them.
654	
655	## Graphics of any other size
656	
657	Any other graphic is kept as placed and rescaled from the old canvas, like a title. That includes a graphic with the same area as the canvas but another shape, such as 1080 × 1920 on a 1920 × 1080 canvas.
658	
659	## Templates measured by the short side
660	
661	Every [bundled template](/graphics/templates/) measures itself by the short side of the size it draws at, so it fits a tall frame. Older copies of these six measured by the height instead:
662	
663	- Lower third
664	- Title card
665	- Callout
666	- Bar chart
667	- Counter
668	- Kinetic type
669	
670	The current six draw exactly as those older copies did on a landscape or square canvas.
671	
672	## Older template copies
673	
674	A project can hold an older copy of one of those six, inserted before they measured by the short side. Frame Job looks at every module a clip draws, on the timeline and inside nests, and recognises these by their text, never their name. A copy you renamed `intro` is still found.
675	
676	What happens next depends on **Make a copy** in the Make Vertical Version sheet:
677	
678	| **Make a copy** | What happens |
679	| --- | --- |
680	| Ticked | The copy that opens has each older module rewritten with the current template. Your earlier text is kept as the module's previous version, so [File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…](/graphics/manage-graphics/) brings it back. The project you started from never changes. |
681	| Unticked | Nothing is rewritten, and the summary names each module. |
682	
683	## Your own modules
684	
685	A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height, with `ctx.height / 1080` in its text, is named in the summary, because it may not fit the narrow frame. This applies with or without **Make a copy**, and the module is never rewritten.
686	
687	A template you've edited counts as your own, since its text no longer matches any template Frame Job shipped.
688	
689	To fix one of these, measure by the short side instead:
690	
691	```js
692	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
693	```
694	
695	On a landscape canvas that's the same number as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a tall canvas drawing the graphic 1.78 times too big. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
696	
697	## What the summary says
698	
699	The sheet's summary reports all of this before you choose **Make**, and it stays accurate as you change the sheet. The exception is while it says it will find faces, people and shot changes first: that summary lists none of this.
700	
701	| The summary says | What it means |
702	| --- | --- |
703	| "Re-sizes 2 graphics to the new canvas." | That many canvas-sized graphics are being re-sized. |
704	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | That many older template copies are rewritten in the copy. |
705	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." | You've unticked **Make a copy**. Tick it to update the module. |
706	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it sizes itself by the canvas's height, so it may not fit the narrow frame." | Check this graphic on the new canvas. |
707	
708	## With an agent
709	
710	[`make_vertical_version`](/mcp/tools-framing/#make_vertical_version) reports the same things in `graphics` when it finishes: how many graphics it re-sized, the modules it updated, and each module it left as it is, with the reason. See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
711	
712	## Related
713	
714	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
715	- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
716	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
717	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
718	---
719	title: "Animate graphic properties"
720	description: Use an action to move a graphic's numbers and colours over time, switch its text and pictures at a set moment, and keep some properties out of the animation.
721	---
722	
723	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
724	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
725	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
726	
727	A graphic's [properties](/graphics/properties/) can change over time, in the same way an [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip's position or fades its opacity. Use this to slide a bar's size, change an accent colour, or swap a line of text part way through a clip.
728	
729	<AtAGlance
730	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
731	  keys="⌥⌘K"
732	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, with an action selected"
733	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_graphic']}
734	/>
735	
736	## Animate with an action
737	
738	<Steps>
739	
740	1. Select the graphic clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>).
741	
742	2. With the action selected, open the **Graphic** sub-tab.
743	
744	3. In **Properties**, set the values the graphic should end at. Each row you change gets a ◆.
745	
746	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the change.
747	
748	</Steps>
749	
750	<Shot
751	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
752	  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a count of 3. The accent, size and boxed rows have a diamond in their gutter, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
753	/>
754	
755	While an action is selected, the **Properties** rows edit the action's end, not the clip. A value you set is kept as you set it, even when it equals the module's default. **Size** and **Timeline** always edit the clip, and they show ⊘.
756	
757	The graphic gets the current values on every frame, and any animation the module does for itself still runs on top.
758	
759	To stop animating a property, take it out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action). To change when the action runs, how long it takes or its curve, see [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
760	
761	## What ramps
762	
763	Numbers and colours move along the action's curve from start to end.
764	
765	**A number** arrives with decimals. Going from 64 to 129, it's 96.5 halfway, and it's never rounded or snapped to the property's step.
766	
767	**A colour** blends through OKLab, which keeps the middle of the blend clean, and its transparency blends as a separate value. `#ff0000` to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, and `#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, a half-transparent grey.
768	
769	While a property moves, every frame has to be drawn anew. A graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
770	
771	:::caution
772	A module that needs whole numbers has to round them itself, or mark the property [`animate: false`](#stop-a-property-animating). One that does neither can fail on a fraction, and `new Array(props.count)` is the usual case. Those frames draw the error card, and an export stops there.
773	:::
774	
775	## What switches
776	
777	Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures can't blend. They hold their value through the action, then change to the end's value as the action ends. Their rows say "at end".
778	
779	For a picture, choosing **None** in the pop-up means no picture from the end of the action.
780	
781	## Where an animated property starts
782	
783	An action starts from the value in force when it begins. That's the clip's own value, or what an earlier action finished on.
784	
785	If the clip holds no value for a property, the first action to name it starts from the module's default at that moment. That default is written into the clip in the same undo step, so changing the default later doesn't move the animation. A picture property with no default starts with no picture.
786	
787	Resetting the clip's own value for a property an action animates sets it to the default, so the action still has somewhere to start from.
788	
789	## Stop a property animating
790	
791	A module can mark any property with `animate: false`, and you can't then make an action animate it. It's for anything a ramp would break, such as a count, a layout mode or a data series. The bundled templates use it for counts and data series.
792	
793	The property's row shows ⊘, and it edits the clip even while an action is selected.
794	
795	If you write modules, it's one more key on the schema entry. It must be `true` or `false`, and anything else stops the module compiling. Leaving it out means `true`.
796	
797	```js
798	export const schema = {
799	  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1, animate: false },
800	};
801	```
802	
803	See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) or **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.
804	
805	## Values and the module
806	
807	Each value you put in an action is checked against the module as it is now, including any minimum and maximum, and one that doesn't fit isn't accepted. That has a few effects when the module changes after you've animated it:
808	
809	- A value already stored isn't checked again, so narrowing a range later leaves the old end value in place.
810	- If an action names a property the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate, the row shows dimmed with **⌫**. Choose it to take the property out of the action.
811	- While the module is missing or won't compile, the **Properties** section has no rows to edit, and reads "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." You can still take values out of the action with **⌫**.
812	
813	## The badge
814	
815	The **Graphic** sub-tab shows a **◆N** badge counting how many properties the selected action animates. The **Properties** section header shows the same count. See [Read the sections and sub-tabs](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-sections-and-sub-tabs).
816	
817	On the timeline, an action's band names a graphic's animated properties along with anything else the action changes, when the track is tall enough to show the label.
818	
819	## With an agent
820	
821	An agent works the same way. It calls [`add_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#add_action), then [`set_action_end`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end) with the end values as `{graphic: {props: {…}}}`. A property set to null comes out of the action, and `graphic: null` takes them all out. It never sends the module's schema, because Frame Job reads that itself.
822	
823	It can't set a value on a property marked `animate: false` that way, and sets it on the clip with [`set_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#set_graphic) instead. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#animating-graphic-props).
824	
825	## Related
826	
827	- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
828	- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
829	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
830	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
831	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
